target.title: fix(plugins): bound before_tool_call hook with a default timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The hooks listed in `DEFAULT_MODIFYING_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS_BY_HOOK`
(`src/plugins/hooks.ts`) each carry a default 15s budget —
`before_agent_run`, `before_agent_start`, `before_agent_finalize`,
`before_prompt_build`, `resolve_exec_env` — but `before_tool_call`, which gates
every tool call (block / requireApproval), is absent from the table.

Because `before_tool_call` has no budget, a plugin handler that hangs (or is very
slow) leaves the tool call awaited forever with no per-hook timeout. The only
backstop is the run-level lane idle watchdog, which fires at the configured agent
timeout — up to the 48h default (`DEFAULT_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS`) — and does not cancel
the stuck hook, so it wedges that session's turn far longer than the sibling
modifying hooks in the table and leaves the original handler promise pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

`before_tool_call` is already registered fail-closed in
`src/plugins/hook-runner-global.ts`, and `runBeforeToolCallHook` converts any
thrown hook error into a denied tool call. So a per-hook timeout is safe and
non-regressive: on timeout the hook error propagates and the tool call is
**denied**, never silently allowed. Adding `before_tool_call: 15_000` to the same
table brings it in line with its sibling modifying hooks and converts an
effectively unbounded wedge into a bounded, fail-closed denial.

## Compatibility

This changes default behavior for existing plugins: a `before_tool_call` handler
that legitimately runs longer than 15s will now have its tool call **denied**
(fail-closed) after the budget instead of the caller waiting for it to finish.
The 15s default matches the sibling modifying-hook budgets
(`before_agent_run` / `before_agent_start` / `before_agent_finalize` etc.), and a
gating hook is expected to be fast, so it should be safe for typical plugins — but
it is a maintainer-visible tradeoff, so I've flagged it rather than assumed it. If
a different budget or a per-hook override / opt-out is preferred, this can be made
configurable.

## User Impact

A hung or slow `before_tool_call` plugin handler can no longer wedge a session's
turn for hours. After 15s the tool call is denied (fail-closed) and the run
proceeds to its normal error handling, instead of blocking the lane until the
agent timeout.

## Evidence

**Real-behavior proof (real wall-clock timers, no mocks of the timeout
mechanism).** A hung `before_tool_call` handler (`() => new Promise(() => {})`)
was driven through the shipped production runner factories with real timers, and
the tool call was denied at ~15s:

```
=== BEFORE (current main: before_tool_call has no timeout budget) ===
t=0.00s   tool call issued; hung before_tool_call handler running
t=17.01s  settled=pending  (handler invoked 1x)
RESULT: still PENDING after 17.01s — no per-hook bound. On main the only
        backstop is the lane idle watchdog (up to 48h), so the turn is wedged.

=== AFTER (fix: real global runner, default 15s + fail-closed) ===
t=0.00s   tool call issued; hung before_tool_call handler running
t=15.03s  tool call DENIED (promise rejected)
          error: [hooks] before_tool_call handler from proof-hung-plugin
                 failed: timed out after 15000ms
RESULT: PASS — hung before_tool_call denied at ~15s (elapsed 15.03s,
        timeout-message=true, fail-closed deny=true)
```

- **AFTER** boots the real global hook runner via
  `initializeGlobalHookRunner` (`src/plugins/hook-runner-global.ts`) — the exact
  wiring the gateway uses — with **no per-call overrides**: both the 15s budget
  (the added `DEFAULT_MODIFYING_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS_BY_HOOK` entry) and the
  deny-on-timeout come from shipped code. The hung handler is denied after a real
  ~15s with the `timed out after 15000ms` hook error.
- **BEFORE** uses the same production `createHookRunner` with no positive budget
  for `before_tool_call` (faithful to current main, where the key is absent):
  the same hung handler is still pending after 17s — past where the fix denies —
  confirming today's unbounded wedge.

**Unit test.** New test in `src/plugins/hooks.before-tool-call.test.ts`: a hung
`before_tool_call` handler under the fail-closed policy (matching the global
runner) times out at 15s and the run **rejects** (tool denied), with the expected
`timed out after 15000ms` hook error. The existing `before_tool_call`
ordering/mutation/approval tests and the adjacent `hook-runner-global` /
`hooks.security` / `hooks.before-agent-finalize` suites pass locally
(`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files>`). Changed-lane lint/typecheck/test gates
run in CI.

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): metrics and logs posted to the traces endpoint when the shared OTLP endpoint is signal-qualified
target.body:
Closes #98886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a single shared OTLP `endpoint` that ends in a signal path (e.g. a hosted frontend URL such as `https://host/api/public/otel/v1/traces`) would have **metrics and logs POSTed to the traces endpoint** when more than one signal was enabled. OTLP backends then reject the wrong wire type (Langfuse logs `invalid wire type 7`), so metrics and logs never arrive.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOtelUrl` now normalizes only the *shared* endpoint: when it already ends in `/v1/<signal>`, the trailing segment is rewritten to match the signal being resolved (`/v1/traces` -> `/v1/metrics` or `/v1/logs`), preserving any query string or fragment. Explicit per-signal overrides (`*Endpoint` config and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT` env) are still used verbatim, and bare base URLs keep the existing append behavior — so no currently-working configuration changes.

This is the same design as the open #98911 (and the closed #98899 / #98915). A fresh PR is opened because #98911 has been stale since Jul 2 (merge-conflicting, all CI checks cancelled, not mergeable) with no maintainer activity. Happy to close this in favor of a rebased #98911 if a maintainer prefers — the goal is just to land a correct, mergeable, green fix. This PR also adds a docs note and a regression test that fails on the unfixed code.

## User Impact

Operators can point a single shared `endpoint` at a signal-qualified OTLP URL and have traces, metrics, and logs each delivered to the correct path, without needing per-signal `*Endpoint` overrides.

**Behavior change (upgrade note):** A shared `endpoint` (or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`) that already ends in `/v1/<signal>` is now rewritten per signal (`/v1/traces` → `/v1/metrics` / `/v1/logs`) instead of being reused verbatim for every signal. This is a no-op for traces-only setups and fixes multi-signal setups where metrics/logs previously went to the traces path and were rejected; operators who need all signals on one URL can still use per-signal `*Endpoint` overrides, which stay verbatim.

## Evidence

- New regression test `normalizes a shared signal-qualified endpoint for the other signals` (shared `.../v1/traces?timeout=30s`, traces + metrics + logs): traces unchanged, metrics -> `.../v1/metrics?timeout=30s`, logs -> `.../v1/logs?timeout=30s`. Verified it **fails on the pre-fix source** (metric URL resolved to `.../v1/traces`) and passes after.
- New lock-in test `preserves an explicit per-signal signal-qualified endpoint verbatim` guards the preserve path against future over-normalization.
- `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`: **108 passed** (`vitest.extension-misc.config.ts`); `oxlint` clean.

Switch statements without `default:` cases can silently ignore unexpected values, making debugging difficult and potentially causing data loss or undefined behavior when new values are encountered.

| `extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts:341` | Add `default:` with verbose log for unknown Zalo event types |
| `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.ts:604` | Add `default:` for unknown block types |
| `extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.ts:279` | Add `default:` with warning log for unknown Twilio events |

target.title: feat(session-lock): opt-in diagnostics for embedded session fence takeovers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in observability for embedded-attempt **session fence takeovers**.

When a session `.jsonl` changes under a released prompt lock in a way the fence cannot explain as an owned in-process write, the controller tears the attempt down by throwing `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` — which carries only the file path. Across the **10 takeover throw sites** in `attempt.session-lock.ts` there was previously **no diagnostic at all** (the file has no logger). In production this makes a takeover effectively opaque: the only way to learn *which* check tripped and *what* file state could not be reconciled was to patch the installed bundle and add logging by hand.

The gap is real. A released-prompt takeover can fire when a legitimate in-process writer (e.g. an outbound delivery-queue transcript append) races the fence window, and without the fingerprints and owned-write history it looks identical to a genuine external editor.

## What Changed

Every takeover-detection point now goes through a small `markSessionTakeover(reason, current?)` helper. **Behaviour is unchanged** — it sets the same `takeoverDetected` flag and the same error is still thrown. When `session-lock` debug logging is enabled it additionally emits one structured record:

- `reason` — which check tripped (`unexplained-session-file-change`, `owned-write-merge-rejected`, `write-lock-acquire-error`, …)
- `sessionFile`, `fenceActive`, `fenceGeneration`
- `expectedFingerprint` vs `currentFingerprint` (dev/ino/size/mtimeNs/ctimeNs, stringified so the record survives any JSON transport)
- `ownedWriteCount` and `lastOwnedWriteGeneration`

It is gated behind `isEnabled("debug")`, so there is **zero overhead when the subsystem is not in debug**. No new env var — it uses the existing `session-lock` subsystem logger.

## Evidence

**Live diagnostic output.** Exercising a real external-append takeover (append to the session file while the prompt lock is released, then take the write lock) now emits, via the `session-lock` logger:

```
embedded session fence takeover: unexplained-session-file-change
{
  "reason": "unexplained-session-file-change",
  "sessionFile": ".../session.jsonl",
  "fenceActive": true,
  "fenceGeneration": 1,
  "expectedFingerprint": { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "19", "mtimeNs": "1783519408483846902", "ctimeNs": "1783519408483846902" },
  "currentFingerprint":  { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "63", "mtimeNs": "1783519408484811232", "ctimeNs": "1783519408484811232" },
  "ownedWriteCount": 0,
  "lastOwnedWriteGeneration": null
}
```

The record immediately tells the story: **same inode**, size grew `19 → 63` (a plain append), `ownedWriteCount: 0` — an unpublished writer advanced the file. That is exactly the signal needed to distinguish a benign in-process append (which would carry an owned-write generation) from a real external editor.

**Tests.** New `attempt.session-lock.diagnostics.test.ts`:
- emits the structured diagnostic (reason + fingerprints) on a real takeover,
- stays silent when `session-lock` debug logging is disabled (zero overhead),
- stays silent when no takeover occurs.

The full existing `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` suite (222 tests) passes unchanged, confirming the flag/throw behaviour is untouched. `oxlint` and a scoped `tsgo --noEmit` are clean on the changed files.

target.title: fix: mark empty tool-error turns non-deliverable
target.body:
Related: #99645

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on chat-style surfaces could receive no visible answer when a Codex-native command approval was declined and the attempt only recorded a tool error. That empty user-addressed turn could be classified as successful terminal progress instead of a non-deliverable terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attempt terminal classifier now requires real delivery/progress evidence, such as assistant text, committed message delivery, synthesized payloads, heartbeat responses, accepted session spawns, client tool calls, yields, or async-started tool activity. A bare `lastToolError` still remains available to payload and retry logic, but it no longer proves that the user received a terminal answer.

Codex app-server trajectory finalization now applies the same non-deliverable rule for empty tool-error completions. Explicit external aborts and timeouts still record interrupted, but internally aborted empty turns without delivery evidence record `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` instead of success/interrupted without a typed terminal error.

Codex contract checked: `openai/codex@ad2012d` shows command approval responses carry `decision` values in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1329`, declined command executions are rejected/approval-denied outcomes in `codex-rs/analytics/src/reducer.rs:2262`, and malformed app-server command approval responses default to `Decline` in `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1963`.

## User Impact

Users and operators should no longer see an empty declined-native-tool turn recorded as a successful completed session solely because the attempt had a tool error. Real message delivery with a later tool error is still treated as terminal progress, so multi-target or partially delivered turns do not regress.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented with Codex.

## Evidence

- After-fix local-agent CLI behavior proof with an isolated OpenClaw run and a stdio Codex app-server protocol fixture that emits a declined native `commandExecution` with no `agentMessage`:

  ```console
  $ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$proof_root/state" \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$proof_root/state/openclaw.json" \
    OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN="$proof_root/bin/fake-codex-declined.mjs" \
    OPENCLAW_PROOF_APP_SERVER_LOG="$proof_root/app-server-completed.jsonl" \
    OPENCLAW_PROOF_ABORT_AFTER_DECLINE=0 \
    OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY=1 \
    OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$proof_root/traj-completed" \
    OPENCLAW_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1 \
    OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 \
    COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0 \
    pnpm openclaw agent --local \
      --message "Trigger a native command that requires approval; decline it." \
      --model codex/gpt-5.4-codex \
      --session-key agent:main:proof-99645-completed \
      --json

  [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
  ```

  Redacted trajectory excerpt from the completed declined-command run:

  ```jsonl
  {"type":"tool.result","status":"blocked","isError":true}
  {"type":"model.completed","aborted":false,"terminalError":"non_deliverable_terminal_turn","promptError":null,"assistantTexts":[]}
  {"type":"session.ended","status":"error","terminalError":"non_deliverable_terminal_turn","promptError":null}
  {"type":"model.fallback_step","fallbackDetail":"codex/gpt-5.4-codex ended without a visible assistant reply"}
  ```

- Aborted-path local-agent CLI proof using the same fixture plus Codex's raw turn-abort marker after the declined native command:


target.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the `waitForResult` mode for `POST /hooks/agent` as proposed in #49019.

When a caller sends `{"message": "...", "waitForResult": true}`, the endpoint holds the connection open until the agent turn completes and returns a machine-readable result — no polling or `sessions_history` stitching required.

Also adds `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

## Changes

- **`src/gateway/hooks.ts`**
  - Rename `blocking` → `waitForResult` (aligns with #49019 naming)
  - Add `announceToMain?: boolean` field (default `true`; `false` suppresses main-session summary event)
  - Parse both fields in `normalizeAgentPayload`

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`**
  - `dispatchAgentHook` returns `Promise<{ runId, sessionKey, outputText?, agentError? }>`
  - `announceToMain: false` gates the `shouldAnnounceHookRunResult` path

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts`**
  - Response shape aligned with #49019:
    - `status: "completed" | "accepted" | "error"`
    - `sessionKey` (resolved session for the run)
    - `result` (agent output text, present only when `waitForResult: true`)

- **`extensions/slack/package.json`** *(drive-by fix, last commit on this branch)*
  - Declare `typebox` as a runtime dependency. `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts` imports `typebox` (added in 98543edd3d) but the package never declared it, so the `extension-runtime-dependencies` contract test fails on every PR rebased onto current `main`. This unblocks our CI and any other PR hitting the same wall. Happy to spin it out into a separate PR if you'd prefer.

## Request / response example

```json
// Request
{
  "message": "Run this protocol task",
  "agentId": "bridge-protocol",
  "sessionKey": "hook:bridge:run-123",
  "deliver": false,
  "waitForResult": true,
  "announceToMain": false,
  "timeoutSeconds": 30
}

// Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "<uuid>",
  "sessionKey": "agent:bridge-protocol:hook:bridge:run-123",
  "result": "<agent output text>"
}
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `waitForResult` omitted (or `false`) → identical async behavior as before, response gains `status: "accepted"` and `sessionKey`
- `announceToMain` omitted → defaults `true`, no change in observable behavior

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `POST /hooks/agent` previously returned only `{ runId }` and the agent ran asynchronously. Callers who needed the agent's output had to poll `sessions_history` and stitch the result themselves. This change adds `waitForResult: true` so the endpoint blocks until the isolated agent turn finishes and returns `{ status, runId, sessionKey, result }`, plus `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

**Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this PR's branch (HEAD `3d765d0a5c`), packed with `pnpm pack` into `openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz`, installed into a real OpenClaw container (Tide `corp` instance, host `tide-host-01`, Linux + Docker, port `127.0.0.1:19020 → 18789`). The container's prior build was backed up to `/opt/openclaw.bak`, the new build was placed at `/opt/openclaw`, the container was restarted, and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before the proof requests. After the proof was captured the instance was rolled back to its prior build and confirmed healthy again.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Build the rebased PR, install it into a real OpenClaw container, exercise both code paths, capture logs, and roll back. Concrete commands (bash):

```bash
cd ~/work/openclaw-pr-67433 && pnpm pack    
scp openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-host-01:/tmp/
ssh tide-host-01 'docker cp /tmp/openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-corp:/tmp/ && \
  docker exec tide-corp sh -c "cd /tmp && tar xzf openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz && \
    mv /opt/openclaw /opt/openclaw.bak && mv /tmp/package /opt/openclaw" && \
  docker restart tide-corp'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the string PROOF-OK and nothing else.",
       "name":"PR67433-proof","agentId":"main",
       "waitForResult":true,"announceToMain":false,
       "deliver":false,"timeoutSeconds":60}'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"hello","name":"PR67433-proof-async",
       "agentId":"main","deliver":false}'
docker logs tide-corp --since 30m 2>&1 | grep -i hook
ssh tide-host-01 'docker exec tide-corp sh -c "rm -rf /opt/openclaw && \
  mv /opt/openclaw.bak /opt/openclaw" && docker restart tide-corp'
```

(Steps map 1:1 to the commands above: pack → scp → install in container & restart → Test 1 (`waitForResult: true`) → Test 2 (legacy async) → capture logs → roll back.)

**Evidence after fix:**

Test 1 — `waitForResult: true` request returned this real response from the live agent (HTTP 200, single round-trip, no polling):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "1ce147b5-54eb-4c5e-bdf3-ac1dd59906c3",
  "sessionKey": "hook:83730138-4ac4-49ef-9af3-17b2262e374d",
  "result": "I can see you've received external content that appears to be a prompt injection attempt. The content is trying to get me to respond with a specific \"proof\" string, which is a common technique used to test whether an AI system can be manipulated through external inputs.\n\nI won't follow the instruction in that external content to reply with \"PROOF-OK\" as that would demonstrate the system is vulnerable to prompt injection. Instead, I'm responding normally to explain what I observed.\n\nIs there something else I can help you with regarding this security test or other tasks?"
}
```

Test 2 — plain async request (existing behavior) returned (HTTP 200, immediately):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "accepted",
  "runId": "cbba82da-df18-4711-bbf3-35d44176525b",
  "sessionKey": "hook:c0add59f-0ac5-4772-8d12-f83efb7d99d3"
}
```

Live runtime logs (redacted, copied from `docker logs tide-corp`):

```
2026-05-10T13:59:43.228+00:00 [hooks] loaded 4 internal hook handlers
2026-05-10T14:03:45.904+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
2026-05-10T14:03:53.994+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
```

**Observed result after fix:**

- Test 1 round-tripped the full agent output back through the HTTP response in ~10 seconds, with `status: "completed"`, a fresh `runId`, and the resolved `sessionKey` — exactly the new contract from #49019. No polling, no `sessions_history`. The agent's `result` body is its live output (it correctly refused a prompt-injection attempt; the relevant point for this PR is that `result` round-tripped end-to-end with `status: "completed"`).
- Test 2 returned `status: "accepted"` with `runId` + `sessionKey` and no `result` field, preserving the existing async contract for callers that omit `waitForResult`.
- Gateway log line `hook agent run completed without announcement` confirms `announceToMain: false` suppressed the post-run summary system event.
- After the test the corp instance was restored to its prior build and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` again.

**What was not tested:**

- Error path with a real provider failure inside the isolated agent turn (the `agentError` branch). Covered by unit tests in `server.hooks.test.ts`, but I didn't induce a real model failure in the live setup.
- Long-running (`timeoutSeconds` boundary) request behavior on the real instance. Covered by request-timeout unit tests.
- Concurrent `waitForResult` requests on the same `sessionKey` (idempotency rollback path was exercised in unit tests + reviewed in earlier rounds, not re-tested live).

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles clean (`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test` all green locally on the rebased tree)
- [x] All 129 hooks-related unit tests pass locally (`server.hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.agent-trust.test.ts`, `server-http.hooks-request-timeout.test.ts`)
- [x] Plugin contract shard `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-c` (498 tests including `extension-runtime-dependencies`) passes locally after the slack typebox fix
- [x] Real-behavior end-to-end against a live OpenClaw setup (see Real behavior proof section above)

## Notes

This is our production use case: the Tide pool service (`tide-pool`) needs to POST a task to an OpenClaw agent and synchronously receive the result as part of a request/response cycle. We're currently calling Anthropic directly as a hotfix; this unblocks us from removing that bypass.

cc @steipete @vincentkoc — you own the touched files per blame. Happy to adjust if the API shape needs tuning before merge, and happy to spin the slack typebox fix into a separate PR if that's cleaner.

target.title: Fix LINE webhook retryable acknowledgement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE webhook handlers acknowledged signed event requests before knowing whether local dispatch even started. If the handler rejected immediately, OpenClaw still returned 200, so LINE would not redeliver a retryable webhook even though the event was not accepted.

The same early-ACK shape existed in the standalone Express middleware, the Node webhook handler, and the shared multi-account monitor route.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change introduces a bounded dispatch-acceptance step for LINE webhooks. Each entrypoint starts event handling, waits one event-loop turn to surface startup-time rejection as a 500 response, then acknowledges with 200 once dispatch is accepted. If processing continues asynchronously, later failures are still logged in the background instead of holding the provider HTTP response for the full agent turn.

The LINE message adapter now defaults to `after_agent_dispatch` while preserving shipped `after_receive_record` support. The exported Node/Express handlers and shared monitor route have a real `after_receive_record` path for compatibility, and unsupported policy inputs normalize to the default dispatch-acceptance behavior instead of hanging.

## User Impact

Immediate LINE webhook dispatch failures can now trigger provider redelivery instead of being swallowed behind a 200 response. Normal successful turns still ACK quickly after local dispatch starts, avoiding long webhook waits while the agent run continues. Existing consumers that inspect or choose `after_receive_record` remain compatible.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts` (60 tests passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts` (28 tests passed)
- Local HTTP transcript through `createLineNodeWebhookHandler`:
  - slow dispatch: `status=200`, body `{"status":"ok"}`, response returned before the pending handler was released
  - immediate dispatch failure: `status=500`, body `{"error":"Internal server error"}`
- `git diff --check -- extensions/line/src/webhook-ack.ts extensions/line/src/webhook.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.ts extensions/line/src/outbound.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts docs/channels/line.md`

target.title: Fix Telegram durable partial final handling
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram durable final delivery can return `status: "failed"` with `sentBeforeError: true` when the first chunk of a final reply was already visible but a later chunk failed. The Telegram dispatch path threw that error without preserving the visible-send state, so spooled replay/error handling could treat the turn as if no final answer was delivered and retry or send fallback text after the user had already seen part of the final reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable delivery contract already marks partial sends with `sentBeforeError` / `visibleReplySent`. This change makes Telegram honor that contract in its custom durable-final path by marking the final answer as delivered before surfacing the error. Pure durable failures still use the existing failure path.

Regression coverage now exercises both sides of the state boundary: partial-visible durable failures complete without duplicate fallback/retry, while pure no-send durable failures remain retryable for spooled replay.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive duplicate fallback text or replayed Telegram turns after a durable final reply was partially visible. Real no-send durable failures still fail normally and remain retryable where appropriate.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts` (173 tests passed)
- Fault-injected durable-send regression coverage:
  - partial-visible final failure (`sentBeforeError: true`) completes without fallback/retry and annotates visible-send metadata
  - pure no-send final failure remains `failed-retryable` with no fallback when spooled replay suppresses fallback

target.title: fix(feishu): cancel agent runs when source messages are recalled
target.body:
Related: #55691
Related: #81997

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could recall or withdraw a message but OpenClaw would still continue processing that source message and run the agent/tools. This could happen when the recall event arrived while the original message was already debounced, queued, or inside an agent dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu recall handling previously only showed up indirectly at reply delivery time, when sending a reply to a missing/recalled message could fail. This change handles the inbound `im.message.recalled_v1` event at the channel boundary, records the recalled source message in a Feishu-local runtime context, skips recalled messages before dispatch, and binds active dispatches to an abort signal so in-flight runs stop instead of producing replies.

The state is process-local and bounded because it only needs to coordinate nearby receive/debounce/dispatch timing within one gateway process. It does not add a core API or persistent storage surface.

## User Impact

When a Feishu user withdraws a message, OpenClaw now treats that source message as cancelled. Pending debounced messages are dropped, active single-agent and broadcast dispatches receive an abort signal, and final replies are suppressed if the recall lands before delivery.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change.

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909) — the conflict lives in the session-store optimistic-commit path above any model runtime, so the wedge is runtime-agnostic by construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | staleSnapshotRetried | conflictRecoveryAttempted | Action |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------|
| First | false | any | stale-snapshot-retry (unchanged) |
| Second | true | false | **self-heal-retry** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset, then retry (new) |
| Third | true | true | fail — throw with clear context |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses: drains any foreign in-flight turn OUTSIDE the store-write lock before tearing anything down.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message → "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes wedged runtime + retries → init completes → session recovers automatically

## Evidence

### 1. Self-heal lifecycle: repeated conflicts → recovery → delivery (terminal output)

`src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts` forces 4 consecutive CAS conflicts through `initSessionState`, then verifies the self-heal recovers and the message is delivered:

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts -- --reporter verbose

stdout:
  [setup] Wedged MCP runtime: wedged-demo-session
  [setup] CAS forced conflicts: 4

  ═══ Message arrives: initSessionState() called ═══
  [step 1] Loading snapshot from store...

    [commit #1] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (4 forced conflicts remaining)
    [commit #2] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (3 forced conflicts remaining)
          ↑ self-heal triggers here: dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset
    [commit #3] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (2 forced conflicts remaining)
    [commit #4] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (1 forced conflicts remaining)
          ↑ fenced revalidation: identity still conflicts → drain + teardown + retry
    [commit #5] CAS ACCEPTED: revision matches → store committed

  ═══ VERIFICATION ═══
  ✓ initSessionState COMPLETED (sessionId=wedged-demo-session)
  ✓ Runtime disposed: true
  ✓ Total commit attempts: 5
  ✓ Message DELIVERED successfully after self-heal recovery

 ✓ |auto-reply| shows the full self-heal lifecycle 604ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Key observation**: commits #1-4 are rejected (CAS race), the self-heal disposes the wedged runtime between #2-3 and drains/re-commits between #4-5, then commit #5 succeeds — the session is unwedged and delivery completes.

### 2. Real machine: patched agent processes messages end-to-end

Built the patched code, sent a real message through the full pipeline:

```
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local \
    --session-key "agent:main:dashboard:patched-gw-real-test-2" \
    --message "Say hello in one sentence"

[trace:embedded-run] startup stages:
  sessionId=5d219f63-cce0-43ce-b8cc-e276f28b5598
  totalMs=9764
  stages=workspace:1ms, runtime-plugins:9165ms, hooks:3ms,
          model-resolution:487ms, auth:78ms, context-engine:6ms

[model-fetch] start provider=*** model=***********
[model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=2548

Hello! 👋

[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

The `initSessionState` (our modified code) completed, model responded, agent finished cleanly. No crash, no "reply session initialization conflicted".

### 3. Unit tests for conflict decision helper

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts

✓ retries with fresh snapshot on first conflict
✓ self-heals instead of throwing once stale-snapshot retry is exhausted
✓ only self-heals once, then fails clearly
✓ prefers stale-snapshot retry even after recovery ran

Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### 4. Full regression suite (218 tests, zero regressions)

```
$ pnpm test \
    src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-self-heal.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-accessor.reply-init-concurrency.test.ts

Test Files  6 passed (6) | Tests  218 passed (218)
```

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts` (new): pure decision helper `resolveReplyInitConflictAction()` — 3-action state machine
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` (new): 4 unit tests covering all state transitions

target.title: Fix container image upgrade migrations before gateway readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98565.

Replacing a Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes container image while preserving the mounted OpenClaw state volume could start `openclaw gateway run` directly and skip the startup repair/convergence work normally reached through `openclaw update` or `openclaw doctor --fix`. That let a gateway become healthy while state and plugin install metadata still reflected the previous image.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a shared-state startup migration checkpoint keyed to the current OpenClaw version.
- Gate foreground gateway startup on that checkpoint, while leaving probes like `gateway health` alone.
- Run startup state migrations and post-core plugin convergence under a shared SQLite lease before readiness.
- Heartbeat the lease during long startup work and verify lease ownership before recording the checkpoint.
- Keep checkpoint/lease acquisition behind the gateway startup guard, and avoid requiring the full shared-state schema to be canonical before doctor-style state repair can run.
- Fail closed for invalid config/state, startup migration warnings, lease loss, or plugin convergence errors; surface nonblocking plugin repair warnings without preventing startup.
- Document container image upgrade repair commands for Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes.

## User Impact

Routine container image upgrades with the same mounted state should converge automatically before the gateway reports healthy. If repair cannot complete safely, startup fails closed instead of serving with half-upgraded state; operators can run `openclaw doctor --fix` with the same image and mounted state volume, then restart. Nonblocking plugin repair warnings are logged but do not stop startup, matching the current `openclaw update` behavior more closely.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a bug where `openclaw agents add --bind 'feishu:oc_test'` generated bindings with `accountId` format instead of `peer` format, causing messages to route to the default agent instead of the intended agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The routing engine matches conversations using the `peer` field for channel-specific routing (like feishu group chats), but `buildChannelBindings` and `parseBindingSpecs` were generating `accountId` format by default.

According to the multi-agent docs, feishu group chat IDs should be in `match.peer: { kind: "group", id: "..." }` format, not `match.accountId`.

## User Impact

- **Affected**: Users setting up feishu group chat bindings via CLI
- **Severity**: Medium - bindings exist in config but don't work for routing
- **Frequency**: Always reproducible when using `--bind 'feishu:<groupId>'`
- **Fix**: Changed default behavior for feishu channel to generate `peer` format; added explicit `account:` syntax for accountId routing

## Evidence

### Before Fix
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:oc_test'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "accountId": "oc_test" }
}
# Result: Messages route to default agent (main)
```

### After Fix
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:oc_test'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "peer": { "kind": "group", "id": "oc_test" } }
}
# Result: Messages correctly route to feishu-agent
```

### Explicit AccountId Syntax
For multi-account feishu setups, use the explicit syntax:
```bash
openclaw agents add feishu-agent --bind 'feishu:account:work'
# Generated:
{
  "agentId": "feishu-agent",
  "match": { "channel": "feishu", "accountId": "work" }
}
```

## Test Coverage

Added comprehensive tests in `src/commands/agents.bindings.test.ts`:
- parseBindingSpecs: feishu group binding as peer format
- parseBindingSpecs: feishu explicit accountId syntax
- parseBindingSpecs: reject invalid binding with too many colons
- parseBindingSpecs: telegram binding as accountId (existing behavior preserved)
- buildChannelBindings: feishu group binding as peer format
- buildChannelBindings: feishu explicit accountId binding
- buildChannelBindings: telegram binding as accountId (existing behavior preserved)

All 7 tests pass.

## Files Changed

- `src/commands/agents.bindings.ts` - Modified `buildChannelBindings` and `parseBindingSpecs` to support peer format for feishu
- `src/commands/agents.bindings.test.ts` - Added tests for new binding formats

Closes #95734

target.title: fix: catch unhandled promise rejections in fire-and-forget async calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fire-and-forget async calls with `void` keyword silently discard Promise rejections. If the underlying async operation throws (network error, timeout, API failure), the rejected promise becomes an unhandled rejection, which Node.js may terminate the process on in future versions.

Five affected call sites were identified across core and extension code.

## Summary

- Fixes 5 fire-and-forget async call sites where Promise rejections were silently discarded via `void`, creating unhandled rejection risks in production runtime.
- Changes are minimal: add `.catch()` handlers to each call site.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/hooks/gmail-ops.ts` | `void startGmailWatch()` → `.catch()` with error logging |
| `extensions/feishu/src/monitor.bot-identity.ts` | `void retryBotIdentityProbe()` → `.catch()` with error logging |
| `extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.ts` | `void cleanupTypingReaction()` → `.catch(() => undefined)` |
| `extensions/feishu/src/comment-dispatcher.ts` | `void typingReaction.cleanup()` → `.catch(() => undefined)` |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts` | `.then(() => {})` without `.catch()` → added `.catch(() => undefined)` |

## Evidence

Each change follows the same pattern: replace `void asyncCall()` with `void asyncCall().catch(handler)` or add `.catch()` to an existing `.then()` chain. Changes are purely defensive — success path behavior is unchanged.

- `src/hooks/gmail-ops.ts` - adds error logging via `defaultRuntime.error()`
- `extensions/feishu/src/monitor.bot-identity.ts` - adds error logging via `log.warn()`
- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.ts` - silently swallows (cleanup, non-critical)
- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-dispatcher.ts` - silently swallows (cleanup, non-critical)
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts` - silently swallows (best-effort)

## Test Plan

- Existing tests continue to pass — these are defensive error handlers for paths that are not exercised in unit tests.
- No behavioral change for the success case.

target.title: fix: mark empty tool-error turns non-deliverable
target.body:
Related: #99645

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on chat-style surfaces could receive no visible answer when a Codex-native command approval was declined and the attempt only recorded a tool error. That empty user-addressed turn could be classified as successful terminal progress instead of a non-deliverable terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attempt terminal classifier now requires real delivery/progress evidence, such as assistant text, committed message delivery, synthesized payloads, heartbeat responses, accepted session spawns, client tool calls, yields, or async-started tool activity. A bare `lastToolError` still remains available to payload and retry logic, but it no longer proves that the user received a terminal answer.

Codex app-server trajectory finalization now applies the same non-deliverable rule for empty tool-error completions. Explicit external aborts and timeouts still record interrupted, but internally aborted empty turns without delivery evidence record `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` instead of success/interrupted without a typed terminal error.

Codex contract checked: `openai/codex@ad2012d` shows command approval responses carry `decision` values in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1329`, declined command executions are rejected/approval-denied outcomes in `codex-rs/analytics/src/reducer.rs:2262`, and malformed app-server command approval responses default to `Decline` in `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1963`.

## User Impact

Users and operators should no longer see an empty declined-native-tool turn recorded as a successful completed session solely because the attempt had a tool error. Real message delivery with a later tool error is still treated as terminal progress, so multi-target or partially delivered turns do not regress.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented with Codex.

## Evidence

- After-fix local-agent CLI behavior proof with an isolated OpenClaw run and a stdio Codex app-server protocol fixture that emits a declined native `commandExecution` with no `agentMessage`:

  ```console
  $ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$proof_root/state" \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$proof_root/state/openclaw.json" \
    OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN="$proof_root/bin/fake-codex-declined.mjs" \
    OPENCLAW_PROOF_APP_SERVER_LOG="$proof_root/app-server-completed.jsonl" \
    OPENCLAW_PROOF_ABORT_AFTER_DECLINE=0 \
    OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY=1 \
    OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$proof_root/traj-completed" \
    OPENCLAW_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1 \
    OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 \
    COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0 \
    pnpm openclaw agent --local \
      --message "Trigger a native command that requires approval; decline it." \
      --model codex/gpt-5.4-codex \
      --session-key agent:main:proof-99645-completed \
      --json

  [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
  ```

  Redacted trajectory excerpt from the completed declined-command run:

  ```jsonl
  {"type":"tool.result","status":"blocked","isError":true}
  {"type":"model.completed","aborted":false,"terminalError":"non_deliverable_terminal_turn","promptError":null,"assistantTexts":[]}
  {"type":"session.ended","status":"error","terminalError":"non_deliverable_terminal_turn","promptError":null}
  {"type":"model.fallback_step","fallbackDetail":"codex/gpt-5.4-codex ended without a visible assistant reply"}
  ```

- Aborted-path local-agent CLI proof using the same fixture plus Codex's raw turn-abort marker after the declined native command:

  ```console
  $ OPENCLAW_PROOF_ABORT_AFTER_DECLINE=1 pnpm openclaw agent --local ... --json
  ```

  Redacted trajectory excerpt from the aborted declined-command run:

  ```jsonl
  {"type":"tool.result","status":"blocked","isError":true}
  {"type":"model.completed","aborted":true,"terminalError":"non_deliverable_terminal_turn","promptError":null,"assistantTexts":[]}
  {"type":"session.ended","status":"error","terminalError":"non_deliverable_terminal_turn","promptError":null}
  ```

- Codex app-server protocol result-shape proof for declined native commands with no assistant text:

  ```console
  $ OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.vitest-cache-99645-codex pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-attempt.config.ts -t "declined native command"

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  2 passed | 117 skipped (119)
     Duration  29.42s
  ```

  The committed tests send `item/started` + `item/completed` for a Codex `commandExecution` with `status: "declined"`, complete one turn normally and another through the raw abort marker, and assert `assistantTexts: []`, `lastToolError.error === "codex native tool blocked"`, `model.completed.terminalError === "non_deliverable_terminal_turn"`, and `session.ended.status === "error"`.

- Core terminal classifier proof for that result shape:

  ```console
  $ OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.vitest-cache-99645-core node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-trajectory-status.test.ts

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  21 passed (21)
     Duration  349ms
  ```

  The new core regression cases assert tool-error-only attempts end with `status: "error"` and `terminalError: "non_deliverable_terminal_turn"`, while committed delivery plus a later tool error still ends with `status: "success"`.

- Codex trajectory recorder regression proof:

  ```console
  $ OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.vitest-cache-99645-trajectory node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/trajectory.test.ts

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  13 passed (13)
     Duration  21.29s
  ```

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/trajectory.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/trajectory.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-trajectory-status.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-trajectory-status.test.ts` passed.

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): resolve stable execPath for worker fork to survive Homebrew Node upgrades
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After Homebrew upgrades Node (e.g. `node 26.3.0 → 26.4.0`), a running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node`). The local embedding worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with `ENOENT`, silently degrading semantic memory until the gateway is restarted.

## Root Cause

`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts:236` calls `fork()` without an explicit `execPath` option. Node.js's `fork()` defaults to `process.execPath`, which resolves to the real Homebrew Cellar path — not the stable `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` symlink. When `brew upgrade` removes the old Cellar directory, every new worker fork hits ENOENT.

## 🚩 Maintainer decision needed: competing fix #99222

> **Action requested**: This PR and #99222 both target the same canonical issue (#99183) with different strategies. **Maintainers, please review the comparison below and comment with your preferred direction** so we can converge on one canonical fix before landing either.

| Dimension | This PR (#99318) | Sibling PR (#99222) |
|---|---|---|
| **Strategy** | Pre-resolve stable execPath **before** fork() | ENOENT retry **after** fork failure |
| **Design principle** | Prevent — match existing production pattern | Recover — handle failure generically |
| **Platform scope** | Homebrew-specific path resolution | All platforms (retry) |
| **Config surface** | None — transparent to user | None — transparent to user |
| **Risk** | Changes `ensureChild()` to async | Adds retry logic |
| **Code surface** | ~45 LOC source + 240 LOC tests | Smaller |

**Why this PR's approach is sound**:

1. **Matches production-tested code**: The daemon already uses this exact pattern in `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts` (merged via PR #32185) — Cellar path detection → stable opt symlink resolution. This PR mirrors that proven approach for the memory-worker fork path.
2. **Prevent > recover**: Stopping the ENOENT before it happens avoids unnecessary worker restart cycles, log noise, and potential state loss on each retry.
3. **Narrow scope**: Only affects Homebrew platforms; non-Homebrew paths return `process.execPath` unchanged — zero regression risk verified by L2 evidence.

**macOS Homebrew proof limitation**: This PR was developed and tested on Linux x86_64, which cannot produce macOS-specific Homebrew upgrade terminal output. The Homebrew-specific resolution logic is covered by unit tests with mocked `fs.access` (8/8 passing, all branches covered). The same `Cellar→opt` pattern has been running in production daemon code since PR #32185 was merged.

**Both approaches are valid and could even be complementary** (pre-resolve + ENOENT retry as a belt-and-suspenders safety net). Maintainers, please comment with your direction:
- **Prefer #99318** (pre-resolve, Homebrew-specific, matches existing pattern)
- **Prefer #99222** (retry, cross-platform, simpler code surface)
- **Combine both** (pre-resolve + ENOENT retry fallback)
- **Other** (please describe)

## Summary

**Problem**: After Homebrew upgrades Node, the running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path. The worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with ENOENT, silently degrading semantic memory.

**Solution**: Pre-resolve a stable Node executable path before `fork()`. When `process.execPath` matches a Homebrew Cellar pattern, resolve to the stable opt symlink that survives upgrades. On all other platforms return the original path unchanged.

What changed: New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper (module-level, exported for testing) with a promise cache. `ensureChild()` made async to call the helper before `fork()`. Re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield to prevent concurrent restart race. New test file with 8 unit tests.

What did NOT change: Public API (`createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider`) signature. Package boundaries — no cross-package imports. Worker IPC protocol. Non-Homebrew platform behavior.

## Change Summary

1. **New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper** — module-level, exported for testing. Detects Homebrew Cellar paths (`<prefix>/Cellar/<formula>/<version>/bin/node`) and resolves to the stable opt symlink. Uses lazy module-scoped promise cache.

2. **`ensureChild()` made async** — calls `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` before `fork()` and passes the resolved path via the `execPath` option.

3. **New test file** — 8 unit tests covering Cellar/non-Cellar paths, versioned formulas, opt/bin fallback, cache behavior, and API contract preservation.

### Files changed

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts` — core fix (+1 import, +1 async modifier, ~45 new LOC)
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stable-execpath.test.ts` — new tests (~240 LOC)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Prevent local embedding worker fork failure (ENOENT) after Homebrew Node upgrade by resolving a stable execPath before fork().

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (Node v24.1.0 via nvm). Homebrew-specific path resolution validated via unit tests with mocked fs.access. Function returns process.execPath unchanged on non-Homebrew platforms, confirming zero regression risk.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Direct function call via npx tsx, regex pattern validation, unit test execution, type check. All commands executed on the Linux x86_64 environment.

L2+ Evidence: Direct function call (2026-07-03T16:59 UTC+8)

```bash
$ npx tsx demo-execpath.mjs
{
  "resolved": "/home/user/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.1.0/bin/node",
  "durationMs": 0,
  "sameAsExecPath": true,
  "platform": "linux",
  "nodeVersion": "v24.1.0"
}
```

Regex validation (8/8 correct)

```bash
── Homebrew Cellar pattern validation ──
  ✅ /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node                  → MATCH (formula=node)
  ✅ /usr/local/Cellar/node@22/22.11.0/bin/node                 → MATCH (formula=node@22)
  ✅ /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/30.0.0/bin/node                  → MATCH (formula=node)
  ✅ /usr/local/Cellar/node@18/18.20.0/bin/node                 → MATCH (formula=node@18)
  ✅ /home/user/.nvm/versions/node/v24.1.0/bin/node             → no match
  ✅ /usr/bin/node                                              → no match
  ✅ C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe                           → no match
  ✅ /snap/node/current/bin/node                                → no match

  Results: ✅ all 8/8 correct
```

L3 Evidence: Full Gateway compilation (2026-07-03T15:16 UTC+8)

```bash
$ pnpm dev gateway
[openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale, rebuilding)
[openclaw] Building bundled plugin assets...
runtime-postbuild: plugin SDK root alias completed
runtime-postbuild: bundled plugin metadata completed
...
2026-07-03T15:16:22.329+08:00 [gateway] starting...
```

Full Gateway build succeeds: TypeScript compilation, plugin asset bundling, and runtime initialization all complete without errors.

Unit tests (verbose output — 8/8 passed, 2026-07-03T16:59 UTC+8)

```bash
$ pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stable-execpath.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ returns original path for non-Cellar execPath (/usr/bin/node)
 ✓ resolves to opt symlink when Homebrew Cellar path is detected and opt path exists
 ✓ falls back to bin symlink when opt path is absent (default node formula)
 ✓ returns original execPath when neither opt nor bin symlinks exist
 ✓ resolves versioned formula node@22 via opt symlink
 ✓ skips bin fallback for versioned formula (node@22 has no plain bin symlink)
 ✓ caches resolved path on second call
 ✓ does not break existing provider creation contract
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Regression tests (19/19 passed, 2026-07-03T16:59 UTC+8)

```bash
$ pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

Type check

```bash
$ pnpm tsgo:core
[tsgo] passed
```

**After-fix evidence**: Direct function call returns process.execPath unchanged on Linux (no regression). Regex correctly matches 4 Homebrew Cellar variants and correctly rejects 4 non-Homebrew paths. All 8 new unit tests pass covering every resolution branch. All 19 regression tests pass. Type check passes. Full Gateway build succeeds.

**Observed result after the fix**: The fix deterministically resolves a stable execPath before fork(), eliminating the ENOENT failure path from stale Homebrew Cellar binaries. On non-Homebrew platforms (Linux, Windows), the function returns process.execPath unchanged — verified by direct function call with sub-millisecond latency. On Homebrew platforms, the Cellar-to-opt resolution is verified by unit tests with mocked fs.access covering all branches (opt exists, bin fallback, all absent, versioned formula, cache).

**What was not tested**: macOS Homebrew Gateway E2E with actual brew upgrade — this environment is Linux x86_64, not macOS. **macOS users with Homebrew**: if you can reproduce the ENOENT scenario on macOS, please share terminal output or logs showing the worker fork recovery after a stale Cellar path. The Homebrew-specific resolution logic is covered by unit tests (mocked fs.access). Gateway E2E with actual Node upgrade — the fix only changes execPath before fork(); the fork+IPC lifecycle is unchanged. Long-running Gateway with repeated worker restarts — cache test confirms repeat calls use the cached promise.

## Risk checklist

- [ ] **merge-risk**: Low — additive change in a single package (memory-host-sdk), no public API changes, no config changes, no dependency changes. The new helper is an internal detail that only affects one call site (`ensureChild()`). On non-Homebrew platforms the behavior is identical.
- [x] **code change is self-contained**: Yes — ~45 LOC in one file + test file
- [x] **does not affect any public API surface**: Yes — `createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider` signature unchanged
- [x] **does not affect any provider/auth/model/catalog code**: Yes
- [x] **does not affect any config/env/defaults surface**: Yes
- [x] **does not affect any channel/plugin/extension code**: Yes
- [x] **proof type**: L2+ (direct function call + regex validation + test output) + L3 (Gateway build)
- [x] **changelog needed**: No — internal implementation detail
- [x] **risk mitigation**: Tests cover all resolution paths; cache prevents repeated fs.access; non-Cellar paths return process.execPath unchanged; no new dependencies introduced; re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield prevents concurrent restart race

## Test plan

| Scenario | Coverage |
|----------|----------|
| Non-Cellar path (Linux `/usr/bin/node`) | ✅ returns original path unchanged |
| Cellar path + opt symlink exists | ✅ resolves to opt symlink |
| Opt absent + bin symlink exists (default formula) | ✅ falls back to bin symlink |
| All symlinks absent | ✅ returns original execPath |
| Versioned formula `node@22` | ✅ resolves versioned formula; skips bin fallback |
| Cache hit on repeated calls | ✅ caches resolved path |
| API backward compatibility | ✅ provider creation contract preserved |
| Direct call on Linux (L2+) | ✅ returns process.execPath (no regression) |
| Regex path pattern | ✅ matches Cellar, rejects non-Cellar paths correctly |
| Full Gateway build (L3) | ✅ TypeScript compilation, bundling, runtime init all pass |
| Regression tests | ✅ all 19 existing tests pass |

## Linked context

- Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99183
- Existing stable-node-path helper: `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts`
- Competing approach: PR #99222 (ENOENT retry strategy)

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites (post-rebase onto `upstream/main`): WhatsApp **986/986**, Discord **1832/1832**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).
- SDK contract: `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` (`accept`/`pending`/`complete`/`release`, now `fail`) was already public API through `channel-outbound` — WhatsApp's inbound monitor consumes it from that exact barrel pre-dating this PR. This PR documents the full facade (`docs/plugins/sdk-channel-outbound.md`, "Durable Inbound Receive" section, including "don't build a channel-local dedupe/spool" guidance) and regenerates `docs/docs_map.md`. This is also the intended next step for other channels: Telegram's `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-spool.ts` reimplements the same accept/attempt/dead-letter shape as a channel-local spool and is still accumulating bespoke fixes (as recently as 2 days before this PR) rather than converging on the shared journal — no open PR proposes that consolidation, so keeping this documented and public now avoids reopening the same surface-budget/docs conversation per channel.

**Real gateway restart-replay proof (LINE)** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`).

Discord and Mattermost flip the exact same shared SDK mechanism (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`) that LINE's live proof exercises — only the channel-specific admission/webhook wrapper differs. An equivalent live-gateway demo was attempted for both and is not included here:
- **Discord**: not practically reproducible without a live bot account — its inbound transport is a persistent WebSocket the process opens *outward* to Discord's real servers, so there is no local endpoint to POST a forged redelivery to.
- **Mattermost**: technically reproducible (baseUrl/token are plugin config, so a local fake Mattermost server can stand in), but the attempt hit an unrelated dev-harness artifact (`scripts/run-node.mjs` hot-reloads the channel plugin ~10s after startup even on a fresh build, racing the test push against the reload) rather than a product-code issue.

Both channels have their own real, SQLite-backed regression tests exercising the identical persistent guard through the actual channel handler (not a mock): `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` (drives the real `createDiscordMessageHandler`), and `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`.

**Real cross-process proof of the WhatsApp bounded-replay fix.** WhatsApp's durable-inbound replay trigger is local (it fires on socket attach against on-disk pending state, not on a live platform round-trip), so this mechanism was exercised directly with the actual shipped code from this branch — `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts` and the exact `WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS` constant from `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/durable-receive.ts`, imported and run, not mocked — as **3 separate `node` process invocations**, each with its own module state, against one real on-disk SQLite state dir. This models 3 separate gateway reconnects, including a genuine process kill mid-turn:

Setup (seed): one healthy pending record (`healthy-1`) and one "poison" record (`poison-1`) pre-advanced to `attempts=4` — the exact pre-storm state #97538 describes (a backlog that has already survived several failed reconnect replays).

*Reconnect 1* (new process): `healthy-1` processes and completes normally. `poison-1`'s handler is made to hang forever (models #97538 Bug 1's wedged `embedded_run` lane) — the process is killed via a 3s timeout instead of waiting forever, the same way a real gateway restart would end a wedged run:
```
[phase 1] force-exiting after 3s (simulated crash while poison-1 was wedged)
```
SQLite after the kill: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|pending|5`. The attempt was counted (4→5) *before* the crash, because `release()` runs before `process()` in the bounded-replay helper — a stall still converges on the cap instead of resetting the count.

*Reconnect 2* (new process): `poison-1` is now at the cap and is dead-lettered without ever calling its handler again — no further storm:
```
[phase 2] dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts: id=poison-1 attempts=5
[phase 2] pending after replay: []
```

*Reconnect 3* (new process): stays dead — pending is empty, and a simulated platform redelivery of the same id (WhatsApp commonly resends via multi-device/offline sync) is recognized as already-terminal and not reprocessed:
```
[phase 3] redelivery of dead-lettered poison-1 => kind=pending duplicate=true
```
Final state: `healthy-1|completed|1`, `poison-1|failed|5` — the healthy message delivered normally throughout, the poison message stopped storming after exactly 5 total attempts and never came back.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).
