- `git diff --check` -> passed.

- Real behavior proof with production `runEmbeddedAgent` path and a temporary local `proof-harness` returning `request_too_large`, using temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `plugins.enabled=false` to avoid user plugin state: blocked payload returned and `lastBlockedRun` persisted in the real session store.

target.title: fix: preserve Telegram bare URL query separators
target.body: Closes #102162 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Telegram users receiving a bare URL with multiple query parameters could see or open an inline-link destination containing a literal `&` when the agent reply was rendered through Telegram HTML/rich formatting. This affected ordinary model replies such as `https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit` when Telegram linkification turned the visible bare URL into an inline HTML link. ## Why This Change Was Made Telegram now leaves bare HTTP(S) URLs containing raw query separators as decoded text instead of wrapping them in an inline `` marker; labelled Markdown links still use inline-link markup and keep attribute escaping. This keeps the fix local to the Telegram formatter rather than changing the shared Markdown renderer or Slack formatting behavior. Risk note: this touches Telegram channel formatting, so the regression tests cover the plain Markdown, rich HTML, and chunked Telegram render paths, plus the labelled-link non-regression; Slack formatter and shared renderer tests were also run to check sibling behavior. ## User Impact Telegram users should receive bare multi-parameter URLs that preserve the intended raw `&` separator after Telegram parses the HTML text, so tapping the URL does not lose the later query parameters. Users can still send labelled Markdown links as before. ## Evidence Before on current main (`4bf70be01a`), the real Telegram formatter produced an inline link whose href and visible label both contained `&`: ```text https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit ``` After this change, the same real formatter entry points keep the bare URL as Telegram HTML text, while labelled links still render as anchors: ```text markdownToTelegramHtml: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit markdownToTelegramRichHtml: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit markdownToTelegramChunks: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit labelled link: edit ``` Telegram Bot API documentation for HTML parse mode says `&` in text must be sent as `&`, and the MessageEntity contract distinguishes normal `url` entities from `text_link` inline links. A live `getMe` check against the configured Telegram Bot API token returned HTTP 200 with `ok: true`; no token or bot identifier is included here. Commands run: ```text node --import tsx -e 'import { markdownToTelegramHtml, markdownToTelegramRichHtml, markdownToTelegramChunks } from "./extensions/telegram/src/format.ts"; const input="https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit"; console.log(JSON.stringify({html: markdownToTelegramHtml(input), rich: markdownToTelegramRichHtml(input), chunked: markdownToTelegramChunks(input,4096).map((chunk)=>chunk.html).join("")}));' node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.wrap-md.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/render-aware-chunking.test.ts extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/format.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts pnpm tsgo:extensions autoreview --mode local pnpm openclaw agent --local --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --session-key agent:default:issue-102162-telegram-url-proof --message 'Reply with exactly this URL and no extra text: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit' --json --timeout 180 pnpm openclaw message send --channel telegram --target 123456789 --message 'https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit' --dry-run --json ``` Focused test result: 3 Vitest shards passed, covering 129 tests total. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed. Autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings. The DeepSeek local agent run succeeded through the embedded OpenClaw harness with provider `deepseek`, model `deepseek-v4-pro`, and final visible text exactly `https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit`. What was not tested: I did not send to a real Telegram chat or tap the client open-link prompt because this checkout has a bot token but no configured safe target chat. Manual follow-up proof is: send the same bare URL through Telegram with `channels.telegram.richMessages: true`, open it in Telegram Desktop or mobile, and confirm the prompt/tap destination shows `?post=100&action=edit` with a raw `&` separator rather than `&action=edit`. Fixes a privacy boundary bug where shared group, channel, scheduled, or delegated team-operation sessions could receive private long-term workspace memory by default when their session key or persisted metadata looked like a private/direct session.

Shared transcripts keep their restrictive stamp through reset, compaction, continuation, tool inventory/invocation, MCP attach lifecycle, and scheduled/operator reconstruction paths. Fixes #102138 — legacy `models.providers.google` blocks silently fail catalog
validation, making all `google/*` models unavailable with 120s idle timeouts.

Older Google provider config blocks lack three fields required by current schema:

target.body: Closes #102162 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Telegram users receiving a bare URL with multiple query parameters could see or open an inline-link destination containing a literal `&` when the agent reply was rendered through Telegram HTML/rich formatting. This affected ordinary model replies such as `https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit` when Telegram linkification turned the visible bare URL into an inline HTML link. ## Why This Change Was Made Telegram now leaves bare HTTP(S) URLs containing raw query separators as decoded text instead of wrapping them in an inline `` marker; labelled Markdown links still use inline-link markup and keep attribute escaping. target.title: fix(agents): add lock release timeout on attempt teardown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run fails abnormally during tool execution (e.g., tool result lost → synthetic transcript repair → run marked as failed), the session write-lock remains held in memory beyond the run's actual lifetime.

The `disposeHeldLockAfterRetainedIdle()` path calls `waitForRetainedLockIdle()`, which blocks indefinitely when `retainedLockUseCount > 0` (a tool execution that will never complete). The `finally` block in `attempt.ts` hangs at `releaseRetainedSessionLock()`, so the lock is never released. The watchdog eventually reclaims it, but only after the full configured `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes for a 15-minute agent timeout).

During this entire window, **all subsequent requests to the same session fail** with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` (60s acquire timeout), even though the owning run is no longer active.

### Observed behavior

```
session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=72859
```

The session remained completely unresponsive for 7+ minutes until the lock file was manually deleted. This exact scenario also hit the author's own session during development of this fix (meta-ironic proof).

## Why This Change Was Made

A single targeted fix: **add a 30-second timeout to the lock release path in the attempt finally block**.

If `releaseRetainedSessionLock()` (specifically, `waitForRetainedLockIdle()`) does not settle within 30 seconds, the finally block completes and execution continues. The lock remains in memory and is reclaimed by the existing watchdog at its configured `maxHoldMs` — no behavioral change to the watchdog itself.

Key design decisions:
- **No watchdog policy changes**: The watchdog continues to honor the configured `maxHoldMs` derived from agent timeout + grace. Compaction and long-running task windows are preserved exactly as configured.
- **Timer hygiene**: The timeout is extracted into a focused helper (`attempt.release-lock-timeout.ts`) that uses `.unref()` to avoid keeping processes alive, and `clearTimeout` in a `finally` block to prevent timer leaks on normal release.
- **Minimal blast radius**: Only the attempt teardown path is affected. Normal runs that release promptly never see the timeout.

## User Impact

Sessions recover from abnormal run failures within **30 seconds + next watchdog cycle (60s)** instead of waiting the full `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes). The fix benefits any scenario where `dispose()` hangs due to stuck tool executions.

## Evidence

**Root cause trace (from real production incident):**
1. Agent run executing `exec` tool → command not found → tool result lost
2. Synthetic error result injected for transcript repair
3. Run terminates but `finally` block hangs at `releaseRetainedSessionLock()`
4. Lock still in `SESSION_LOCKS.heldEntries()` → `heldByThisProcess = true` → orphan-self-pid skipped
5. Watchdog threshold = 17 minutes → session blocked for entire duration

**Real behavior proof:**
This exact bug hit the author's own session during development of this fix. The session (`1fe741b0-c346-413e-b494-93cb26f5df22`) was locked by pid 96661 (same process, alive) for 15+ minutes across multiple attempts to interact:
```
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=435021
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=679231
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=753583
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=942030
```
The lock persisted from ~435s (7 min) through ~942s (15+ min) — consistent with a maxHoldMs of 1,020,000ms (17 min) before watchdog reclaim. With this fix, the teardown timeout would have fired at 30s, allowing the watchdog to reclaim within 1 cycle.

**Test results:**
- `attempt.release-lock-timeout.test.ts`: 4 tests passed ✅ (timer cleanup on normal release + timeout behavior)
- `session-write-lock.test.ts`: 106 tests passed ✅ (no regression to watchdog logic)
- oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors ✅

Fixes #100872

target.title: fix(discord): preserve content-type and skip optimization for animated/WebP images
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Discord media uploads were sending files without a MIME content-type, causing some clients/bots to misidentify the file format. Additionally, WebP images were being converted to JPEG (losing quality) and animated images (GIF, WebP, APNG) were being converted/optimized, destroying animation frames.
- **Why it matters:** Users sending WebP images or animated GIFs/APNGs via Discord and the web provider received degraded or broken output — silent data-loss bugs.
- **What changed:** `toDiscordFileBlob` now accepts and forwards a `contentType` to the `Blob` constructor; `loadWebMediaInternal` skips image optimization for GIF, WebP, and any animated image (detected via sharp's `pages` metadata); a new `isAnimatedImage` helper was added to `image-ops.ts`.
- **What did NOT change:** Non-animated JPEG/PNG optimization paths are unchanged; no other channels are affected.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

target.title: fix(plugins): honor subagent model-override opt-in in interactive sessions
target.body:
Closes #102167

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a plugin calling `api.runtime.subagent.run(...)` with a `provider`/`model` override from an interactive session (webchat/Control UI, TUI, ACP, or any gateway-client-scoped turn) was rejected with "provider/model override is not authorized" even when the operator had explicitly trusted the plugin via `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride: true`. The opt-in was only consulted for clientless background runs, so cost-tiered plugin workflows (e.g. cheap evidence-gathering subagent workers feeding a more capable main session) could not guarantee the worker model from chat sessions — and the documented config knob appeared broken because docs never said it was background-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin-requested subagent overrides are now authorized by exactly two things, in every execution context: genuine admin scope on the calling client, or the operator's per-plugin opt-in (`allowModelOverride` + `allowedModels`). A policy-authorized override rides the dispatched request's client as a copied internal flag so the downstream `agent` gate honors it without leaking authority to the caller's live connection — and that internal flag is deliberately **not** accepted back as caller authority, so an inherited flag on the request scope can never bypass the policy for nested spawns (`allowedModels` bounds the whole spawn tree; this also closes a pre-existing bypass on the background path, where nested spawns under a synthetic flagged client skipped the allowlist). This aligns the subagent surface with `api.runtime.llm.complete`, whose equivalent per-plugin trust config already applies in every context. Defaults are unchanged and fail closed: no config → deny, now with an actionable pointer to the config key.

## User Impact

Operators can trust a plugin to steer subagent model selection once, and it works the same in interactive and background contexts. Plugin authors can build guaranteed-model subagent workers reachable from chat sessions without granting the driving client admin scope.

**Compatibility note (intentional semantic widening of a shipped key):** on shipped releases (e.g. v2026.6.11) the help text scoped `subagent.allowModelOverride` to "background subagent runs" and the runtime enforced that. After this change, operators who already set the opt-in for background jobs also authorize overrides from interactive turns on upgrade, with no config change. The grant stays plugin-scoped (HTTP/webchat callers never gain model control themselves) and `allowedModels`-bounded; help text and docs were rewritten in this PR to state the widened scope. Flagging explicitly for release notes: config/default surface changed — 1 key widened, 0 added, 0 removed. Second intentional behavior change: nested plugin spawns under internally flagged clients (background synthetic runs, `openai-http`/voice-ingress-triggered runs) previously inherited blanket override authority; they now consult the per-plugin policy like any other plugin call.

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts`: trusted plugin + non-admin client → override forwarded and the dispatched client carries `internal.allowModelOverride: true` on unchanged `operator.write` scopes (proves the downstream gate path); untrusted plugin + non-admin client → rejected with the config-pointer error; **inherited internal flag on the scope client + untrusted plugin → still rejected** (pins the non-transitivity of minted authority). Existing fallback-path and admin-client tests updated for the reworded messages and kept green.
- Focused suites: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-narrative.test.ts` → 178 tests passed post-hardening.
- Changed-files gate: `pnpm check:changed` on Blacksmith Testbox → exit 0 (lint, import cycles, repo guards): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28939856076 (first commit) and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28942275771 (hardening commit), both exit 0.
- Multi-agent review pass on this diff (8 finder angles, per-candidate adversarial verification): the privilege-transitivity finding was verified PLAUSIBLE (mechanism confirmed at every static link, reachability timing-dependent on lane drain context) and is fixed by the second commit; confirmed cleanup findings (merge-guard doubling, doc self-contradiction, comment budget, test fixture duplication) are applied.
- Named follow-up (out of scope here): consolidate the duplicated per-plugin model-override policy engines (`subagent.*` in `src/gateway/server-plugins.ts` vs `llm.*` in `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.runtime.ts`), including unifying allowlist canonicalization on `modelKey()` — the two copies already drift on double-prefix suppression.

target.title: feat(android): manage skills from settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR brings the requested Android skills-management path closer to the existing Control UI behavior while keeping Gateway policy as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings from read-only status into a management surface with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable via `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install from Android via `skills.search` / `skills.install`.
- Add an Android pre-install ClawHub audit review dialog before downloading a skill. The dialog resolves and displays:
  - skill name / slug
  - resolved install version
  - author / publisher
  - ClawHub audited safety result
  - security audit URL when provided
- Extend `skills.securityVerdicts` with a bounded explicit `items[]` request shape so clients can request pre-install review verdicts for known ClawHub slug/version pairs.
- Keep the security boundary server-side: Android cannot pass an arbitrary registry URL for verdict lookup; explicit verdict lookups resolve through the configured default ClawHub registry.
- Preserve Gateway trust enforcement: Android may acknowledge non-blocked review-required installs only from the review dialog; blocked/malicious releases remain blocked by Gateway policy.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android skills status and keep the Android README/i18n inventory current.

## Web UI Reference Checked

Reviewed the existing Control UI skills implementation in:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`

Android now mirrors the relevant requested behaviors from the Web UI: installed-skill filtering/status grouping, global enable/disable, ClawHub search/install, and risk-aware install confirmation.

## Gateway/API Notes

- `skills.securityVerdicts` still supports the existing passive installed-skill verdict collection.
- New explicit mode accepts at most 25 `{ slug, version, ownerHandle? }` items.
- Explicit mode skips installed-skill scanning and fetches only the requested default-ClawHub verdict batch.
- Explicit mode projects the same sanitized fields as installed-skill mode; raw `security` payloads are not exposed.

## Summary

AI-assisted PR.

- Problem: OpenAI-compatible embedding providers passed raw query text to instruction-aware embedding models such as Qwen3, Nomic, and mxbai.
- Why it matters: Raw queries produced lower-quality retrieval for instruction-aware embedding models because query embeddings did not match the model's expected retrieval-query format.
- What changed: OpenAI embeddings now apply model-specific query instruction prefixes for query embeddings, while document batch embeddings remain unchanged.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): No embedding defaults, credentials handling, base URL behavior, document embedding inputs, or non-OpenAI providers were changed.

**Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenAI-compatible embedding providers now apply model-specific query instruction prefixes for instruction-aware Qwen3, Nomic, and Mixedbread embedding model families on query embeddings, while document/batch embeddings remain raw.

target.title: fix(ui): normalize Unicode line/paragraph separators in markdown rendering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LLM outputs (especially from GPT-family models) can contain Unicode line separators U+2028 (`LINE SEPARATOR`) and U+2029 (`PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR`). These are valid Unicode line-breaking characters but JavaScript's `split("\n")` does not treat them as line breaks. When tool results or model-generated text containing these characters reach the chat UI, **all content renders as a single unbroken line** instead of being split across multiple lines as the user expects.

### Full data-flow trace

```
Upstream: LLM generates "Result:   - item1   - item2   - item3"
    ↓
Midstream: Gateway stores it as-is (no U+2028/U+2029 normalization in chat path)
    ↓
Downstream: toSanitizedMarkdownHtml() → split("\n") → 1 element → one long line in UI
```

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts:39` already handles this correctly for exec approval display, but the chat message rendering pipeline has no equivalent normalization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add U+2028/U+2029 normalization alongside the existing `\r\n` → `\n` normalization in all five markdown processing entry points in `ui/src/components/markdown.ts`:

| Function | Line | What it does |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `formatTruncatedMarkdownInput` | 698 | Truncated content formatting |
| `isMarkdownBlockArtText` | 715 | Block art detection |
| `toSanitizedMarkdownHtml` | 1351 | Main markdown → HTML entry point |
| `toEscapedPlainTextHtml` | 1407 | Plain text fallback |
| `toStreamingMarkdownHtml` | 1423 | Streaming markdown → HTML entry point |

A shared `LINE_SEP_RE` constant is defined using `String.fromCodePoint(0x2028)` + `String.fromCodePoint(0x2029)` to avoid ` ` escape sequences in the source code, which triggers oxlint parser issues.

## User Impact

Users will see tool outputs and model-generated text containing Unicode line/paragraph separators correctly split across multiple lines in the chat UI, instead of all content rendered as one long unbroken line. All other content (plain `\n`, `\r\n`) is unaffected and renders identically to before.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof — upstream to downstream chain:**

```
$ node /tmp/u2028-test.js
=== Upstream: LLM returns ===
Original: "Found 3 files:   - /etc/hosts   - /etc/passwd   - /etc/shadow"

=== Midstream: stored as-is, split("\n") does not split ===
split("\n") result: 1 line

=== Downstream: UI renders as one long line ===
Rendered: "Found 3 files:  - /etc/hosts  - /etc/passwd  - /etc/shadow"

=== With fix: U+2028/U+2029 normalized to \n ===
After fix: 4 lines
Found 3 files:
  - /etc/hosts
  - /etc/passwd
  - /etc/shadow
```

**Observed result after fix:** U+2028 and U+2029 characters are normalized to `\n` at the markdown entry points, so all downstream `split("\n")` calls produce correct line counts. Content renders with proper line breaks.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end WebSocket chat round-trip with a real LLM provider returning U+2028/U+2029. The normalization is applied at the markdown rendering layer, which is the same code path for all chat content regardless of origin.

## Regression Test Plan

- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All existing markdown rendering behavior preserved — only U+2028/U+2029 chars are additionally normalized ✅
- `node /tmp/u2028-test.js` — confirms 1-line → 4-line fix ✅

## Root Cause

In JavaScript, `"\n"` (U+000A) is the only character recognized by `String.prototype.split()` as a line break. Unicode defines additional line-breaking characters U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) that are semantically equivalent but not handled by `split("\n")`. LLMs (particularly GPT-family models fine-tuned on diverse text corpora) naturally produce these characters in structured output like file listings, code blocks, and markdown.

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts` already handles this pattern — it was simply never applied to the chat message rendering path. This fix extends the same normalization to the markdown rendering pipeline, which is the common entry point for all chat content displayed in the UI.

target.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DeepSeek and Xiaomi OpenAI-compatible users could lose provider prompt-cache hits after the 6.x boundary-aware cache split put per-turn dynamic context into the system prompt.

Closes #94518

Related: #91018, #90583

## Why This Change Was Made

DeepSeek/Xiaomi use prefix-matching cache behavior, so their stable system prefix needs to remain byte-stable across turns. This PR adds `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache`, defaults it on for those providers, keeps only the stable prefix in the system message, and moves the dynamic suffix into the latest user turn so older conversation history stays reusable.

Operators can opt back into normal boundary-aware behavior with `compat: { disableBoundaryAwareCache: false }`.

## User Impact

DeepSeek and Xiaomi users should keep the stable system prompt and prior conversation history cacheable across multi-turn requests instead of invalidating the reusable prefix with each dynamic suffix update.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): stop forwarding embedding dimensions upstream
target.body: ## Summary - Problem: `memory-lancedb` forwarded `dimensions` to every direct OpenAI-compatible embeddings request, which breaks vLLM/NVIDIA-style providers that reject that field. - Why it matters: memory recall/search can fail at embed time for otherwise compatible providers. - What changed: the direct embeddings client now preserves server-side `dimensions` first, then retries without `dimensions` only when the provider clearly rejects that field; the fallback vector is truncated locally to the configured dimension. - Scope boundary: config shape, provider selection, secrets handling, runtime permissions, and migrations are unchanged. ## Change Type - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope - [x] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes none - Related none - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Root Cause - Root cause: the direct embedding wrapper assumed every OpenAI-compatible provider would accept `dimensions`, then passed it straight through upstream. - Missing guardrail: no regression test covered a provider that rejects `dimensions`, or the compatibility requirement that accepting providers still receive server-side `dimensions`. ## Regression Test Plan - Coverage level: Unit test - Target test file: `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts` - Scenarios locked in: - accepting OpenAI-compatible providers receive `dimensions` upstream; - providers that clearly reject the `dimensions` field are retried without it and use local truncation; - unsupported dimension values stay unavailable without a fallback retry; - short fallback vectors return the memory-recall unavailable result instead of rejecting the tool call. - Supplemental local run: ```text $ .\node_modules\.bin\vitest.CMD run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts -t "sends OpenAI embedding dimensions upstream when accepted|retries without OpenAI embedding dimensions and truncates locally when rejected|returns unavailable when fallback embedding is shorter than the configured dimensions|does not retry without dimensions when the provider rejects the dimension value" Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 4 passed | 124 skipped (128) ``` ## User-visible / Behavior Changes Memory recall still uses server-side dimensions for providers that accept them. Providers that reject `dimensions` now work through a retry without that field, as long as they return a vector long enough to truncate locally. ## Diagram ```text Before: memory_recall -> OpenAI-compatible request with dimensions -> provider rejects body.dimensions -> recall unavailable After, accepting provider: memory_recall -> request with dimensions -> provider-sized vector -> store/search After, rejecting provider: memory_recall -> request with dimensions -> provider rejects body.dimensions -> retry without dimensions -> receive full embedding -> local truncation -> store/search ``` ## Security Impact - New permissions/capabilities? No - Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - New/changed network calls? No - Command/tool execution surface changed? No - Data access scope changed? No - If any Yes, explain risk + mitigation: N/A ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: Windows - Runtime/container: local workspace with pnpm - Model/provider: `nvidia/nv-embed-v1` - Integration/channel: `memory-lancedb` plugin through real OpenClaw `ltm search` - Relevant config (redacted): `embedding.baseUrl=https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`, `embedding.model=nvidia/nv-embed-v1`, `embedding.dimensions=4` ### Steps 1. Configured `memory-lancedb` with NVIDIA's OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint and `embedding.dimensions=4`. 2. Initialized an isolated LanceDB database through the real OpenClaw plugin CLI. 3. Ran `openclaw ltm search "openclaw memory proof" --limit 1` against current main. 4. Ran the same command with the fixed branch plugin loaded. 5. Seeded the branch LanceDB database with a 4-dimensional proof vector and reran the branch search. ### Expected 1. Current main fails because it forwards `dimensions` with no fallback. 2. The fixed branch preserves server-side `dimensions` for providers that accept them. 3. For NVIDIA, the fixed branch retries without `dimensions` after the provider rejection and truncates the returned 4096-dimensional embedding locally to 4 dimensions. 4. LanceDB search succeeds with the configured 4-dimensional table. ### Actual - Current main failed with NVIDIA's live provider error: `400 ... Extra inputs are not permitted ... ('body', 'dimensions')`. - The fixed branch succeeded and returned the seeded LanceDB proof row: `proof branch locally truncated NVIDIA embedding dimensions`. - This confirms the compatibility fallback omits `dimensions` after the provider rejects them and uses local truncation before LanceDB search. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [ ] Perf numbers Current in main: After in this branch, empty DB: After in this branch, seeded DB: Earlier targeted regression test screenshot: ## Real behavior proof - Behavior or issue addressed: `memory-lancedb` OpenAI-compatible embeddings preserve server-side `dimensions` for providers that accept that field, while providers that reject `dimensions` can still recall/search memories through a retry without `dimensions` and local truncation of the fallback embedding. - Real environment tested: Windows local OpenClaw source checkout, pnpm workspace, real `memory-lancedb` plugin with LanceDB storage, NVIDIA OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint using a redacted API key, `embedding.baseUrl=https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`, `embedding.model=nvidia/nv-embed-v1`, and `embedding.dimensions=4`. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. target.title: fix(qqbot): bound gateway websocket payloads

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot gateway websocket connections could accept the `ws` client default 100 MiB inbound message window for gateway events.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot gateway frames are JSON control and message events, so the websocket client now uses the same bounded-frame pattern as other channel gateway transports instead of inheriting the broad `ws` default. The QQ gateway websocket docs describe payloads as the `op`/`d`/`s`/`t` JSON envelope shape, not inline binary media: https://bot.q.qq.com/wiki/develop/api-v2/dev-prepare/interface-framework/reference.html

## User Impact

Operators get a tighter QQBot gateway resource boundary while normal gateway events and proxy-agent handling continue to work.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: fix(codex): ungate app-server terminal liveness and fan out poisoned-client retirement
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Track B2 of #101863 — the Codex app-server half of the liveness redesign (#89742, regression of #82681; also #85251, #90673).

One shared app-server client serves every session with the same auth profile + start options (`shared-client.ts` keyed global map). Two verified defects:

1. **Every fast watch is gated by in-flight server→client requests.** `activeAppServerTurnRequests > 0` suppresses the completion-idle (60s), assistant-completion (10s), *and* terminal-idle (30 min) watches. A client that goes silent with a request outstanding (the reported 429-burst shape: `turn/started`, then nothing) is exactly the state no watch can see; the only remaining bound is the whole run budget.
2. **Retiring a poisoned client doesn't fan out.** After a timed-out turn, the shared entry is detached so *future* acquisitions get a fresh client — but sessions already leased on the wedged process keep waiting with nothing to abort them.

### Why This Change Was Made

**Protocol proof (Codex gate).** Inspected sibling `openai/codex` source directly: server→client requests register a oneshot callback and await the client's response (`codex-rs/app-server/src/outgoing_message.rs:272-350`), completely separate from fire-and-forget server notifications (`outgoing_message.rs:589-629`; envelope split in `app-server-transport/src/outgoing_message.rs:21-31`; types in `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs:1199-1252, 1630-1658`). An in-flight request therefore proves nothing about notification liveness in either direction — gating a notification-silence watchdog on the request counter is unsound.

Changes (all in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/`):

1. **Terminal-idle watch ungated** (`attempt-turn-watches.ts`): the 30-minute zero-notification backstop now fires regardless of in-flight requests. Its clock still resets on every real notification, so healthy turns — including ones legitimately waiting on approvals/elicitation — are untouched as long as the server emits anything within the window. The completion-idle and assistant-completion watches keep their request gates: they express turn-completion semantics, which are genuinely indeterminate while a request is being served. No timeout constants changed.
2. **Suspect-client retirement fans out** (`shared-client.ts`, `attempt-client-cleanup.ts`): `retireSharedCodexAppServerClientIfCurrent` gains an explicit `failActiveLeases` mode used only by the timed-out-turn path — it closes the physical client immediately (transport close SIGKILLs the child after 1s), so co-leased attempts hit the existing client-closed retry path and re-run on a fresh client, and pending acquires reject instead of leasing the poisoned process. **Default retirement stays graceful** (detach + close-when-idle): routine one-shot bundle-MCP cleanup and startup-failure paths keep `main`'s behavior — the initial implementation applied immediate-close to all callers, which would have yanked healthy clients from co-leased sessions at every one-shot run end; review caught it and scoped it, restoring `main`'s two graceful-retirement tests verbatim and adding a pin test for the default.

Stated tradeoff: a healthy sibling turn co-leased on a client that another turn timed out gets aborted-and-retried. Intentional — a client suspect enough to deny future sessions should not keep serving current ones — and the failure is retryable, not user-terminal.

### User Impact

- A wedged shared app-server client is now bounded at 30 minutes of true silence instead of the full run budget (up to 48h), even mid-request.
- One poisoned client no longer wedges every co-leased session: siblings fail over to a fresh client automatically.
- No behavior change for healthy clients, isolated-client mode, or routine cleanup paths.

### Evidence

- Protocol citations above from direct `../codex` inspection (`f1affbac`), verified independently by implementer and reviewer.
- Tests: terminal watch fires with requests in flight + zero notifications (previously structurally impossible); does not fire while notifications arrive; completion/assistant gates regression-pinned; fan-out (co-lease sees retryable client-closed failure, pending acquires reject, fresh acquisition gets a new client); graceful-default retirement pinned (leased client survives routine retire, closes on release); isolated-client path unchanged.
- Validation: full `extensions/codex` suite green (96 files / 2005 tests on Testbox; app-server subset 78 files / 1681 tests re-run green after review edits), extensions tsgo + extensions-test tsgo lanes exit 0, oxlint/oxfmt clean.

Part of #101863 (Track B2). Fixes #89742; addresses #85251 / #90673 (same wedge class — will verify against each before closing).

target.title: fix(agents): keep finite LLM idle watchdog under unlimited run budgets
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Track B3 of #101863. Three coupled timeout-semantics defects, all verified in source and one proven live (the wedge in #101910's E2E was built on exactly this coupling):

1. An unlimited run budget (`runTimeoutMs >= MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`) made `resolveLlmIdleTimeoutMs` return `0` — disabling mid-stream stall detection entirely. Users who configure "no timeout" for long tasks silently trade away all liveness: one TCP half-open or provider stall wedges the turn forever.
2. Self-hosted providers (vLLM et al., #85826) got 300s for the first event but only the generic 120s for mid-stream gaps — legitimate batching/scheduling pauses over two minutes killed the call unless the baseUrl happened to be local.
3. `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds: 0` clamped to **1 second** (`Math.max(seconds, 1)`), while the per-run override path defines `0` as unlimited — the same key with opposite semantics depending on position.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The unlimited-budget sentinel now falls through to provider-class idle/first-event defaults instead of `0`: an unlimited budget bounds total cost, not liveness. Explicit `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds` still wins and may exceed the defaults; genuinely local baseUrls keep their existing idle opt-out (prompt-eval silence is normal there).
- New `SELF_HOSTED_LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` aligns self-hosted mid-stream tolerance with the existing 300s first-event allowance. Cloud stays 120s; cron clamps unchanged.
- Config `timeoutSeconds: 0` now resolves to the same unlimited sentinel as the override path. Safe *because of* the first change: unlimited budget no longer implies zero stall detection. The prior behavior (0 silently becoming a 1s budget that kills every turn) is a footgun, not a contract anyone can be relying on.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` timeout table updated (unlimited-budget semantics, self-hosted idle default).

### User Impact

- The "long-task config" (`timeoutSeconds: 0`) becomes safe by default: unlimited run budget with a finite per-class stream watchdog — the exact hang mode reported as "agent hangs mid-task forever" can no longer be configured accidentally.
- Self-hosted/vLLM users stop losing calls to legitimate >120s mid-stream pauses.
- No change for anyone with explicit provider timeouts or local endpoints.

### Evidence

- Resolver matrix traced case-by-case against current `main` (sentinel × explicit/implicit budget × cloud/self-hosted/local × cron) — precedence identical except the three intended changes.
- Tests: extended resolver tables cover sentinel → class defaults (not 0), self-hosted 300s vs cloud 120s, explicit provider timeout precedence, local opt-out unchanged, and `timeoutSeconds` config table (`0 → unlimited`, finite, negative, NaN). Composition test: config `0` + cloud provider = unlimited budget AND 120s idle watchdog.
- Validation: resolver + import-sweep suites (314 tests), `tsgo` core/core-test lanes, oxlint/oxfmt — green on Testbox.

Part of #101863 (Track B3). Fixes #85826; closes the `timeoutSeconds: 0` footgun identified in the #101863 audit (root cause 2).

target.title: fix(qqbot): soft-wrap exec approval command preview for desktop QQ
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Desktop QQ renders fenced code blocks as a single horizontally scrollable line and does **not** soft-wrap long content, while mobile QQ wraps automatically. As a result, a long command in a QQ Bot exec approval preview was only partially visible on desktop, forcing the approver to drag a horizontal scrollbar to read the full command before approving (issue #101979). This soft-wraps the (already length-capped) command preview at a bounded width before it is placed in the code fence, so the whole command is visible on desktop and still correct on mobile.

The wrapping is now **surrogate-safe**: an earlier version could place a wrap boundary between the high and low surrogate of a non-BMP character (e.g. an emoji), splitting it into two lone surrogates that render as replacement characters. Wrapping now never cuts between a surrogate pair.

Closes #101979.

## Summary

- Soft-wraps the shell command shown in QQ Bot exec approval messages so it wraps inside the code block.
- Approvers on desktop QQ can read the full command at a glance instead of dragging a horizontal scrollbar before approving.
- Wrapping is surrogate-pair-safe so non-BMP characters (emoji) crossing the wrap width are kept intact.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.test.ts` — **10 passed** (local), after the surrogate-safety fix:

  ```
  ✓ extension-messaging  extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.test.ts (10 tests) 62ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  10 passed (10)
  ```

- `wrapCommandPreview` unit tests: short lines unchanged, long lines hard-wrapped ≤ width and losslessly round-trip, existing newlines preserved, non-positive width disables wrapping.
- New regression tests: a non-BMP emoji (`U+1F4A9`, a surrogate pair) positioned so the naive width boundary would fall between its high and low surrogate is **not** split — output round-trips losslessly, contains no lone surrogates, and the emoji survives intact. A width-1 edge case with leading surrogate pairs still makes forward progress.
- `buildExecApprovalText` test proves a 120-char command is wrapped so no code-block line exceeds the wrap width.
- Existing UTF-16-boundary truncation test still proves the surrogate pair is not split by the upstream `truncateUtf16Safe(cmd, 300)` cap.

## Notes

- Wrapping is applied after the existing `truncateUtf16Safe(cmd, 300)` cap, so it never lengthens the underlying command content — it only inserts line breaks for display.
- `wrapCommandPreview` is exported for direct unit testing and future reuse.
- **Behavior proof on a real QQ Desktop client** (screenshot/recording of a long approval wrapping in the actual client) requires a human with a QQ Desktop install; it cannot be produced by an automated agent. The change is validated by the focused unit tests above, which assert the exact wrapping/surrogate behavior that drives what the client renders.

target.title: fix(agents): retry transient reads and fail closed when sweeping stale session write locks
target.body:
Related: #100910

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the gateway's startup session-lock sweep (and
`openclaw doctor`) can delete a valid, actively-held session write lock, breaking
mutual exclusion on a session's transcript. When cleanup reads a lock file, any
transient filesystem error (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK/EINTR under load) is collapsed to
a "no payload" result, which reads as a missing PID. Past the 30-second mtime
grace the lock is then removed with no content-identity check — so a transient
read on a live lock (held for up to the 5-minute max hold) deletes it, after
which a second writer can acquire a fresh lock while the original holder is still
writing the same JSONL.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup removal decision (`cleanStaleLockFiles`) now reads each lock through
`readLockPayloadForCleanup`, which (1) retries only transient read errors — the
same `{EAGAIN, EWOULDBLOCK, EINTR}` classifier used for workspace bootstrap reads
in #100910 — and (2) **fails closed**: if the read still cannot complete after
retries, the lock is treated as unreadable and left in place rather than removed.
A malformed/empty but readable lock is still a successful read (payload null,
reclaimable once old), so existing stale-reclaim behavior is unchanged. This is
scoped to the cleanup removal decision only: the fs-safe **acquire** path already
throws on these transient codes and guards stale removal with a content-identity
re-check, so it needs no change, and the acquire-timeout diagnostics readers are
intentionally left as simple non-retrying reads.

## User Impact

Operators no longer risk a transient IO blip (a single spike or a short burst)
during gateway startup or `openclaw doctor` silently deleting a live session lock
and letting two writers race on the same transcript. No API, config, or
success-path behavior change; readable malformed locks are still reclaimed once
old.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — real `openclaw doctor --fix` run

`node --import tsx` drives the **real `noteSessionLockHealth({ shouldRepair:
true })`** (the exact function `openclaw doctor --fix` runs for its "Session
locks" check) over a **real on-disk `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`** whose lock is owned by
a **real live process spawned with an OpenClaw argv**. No mock of
`cleanStaleLockFiles` / ownership resolution / the store — only a single transient
`EAGAIN` is injected at the `fs.readFile` boundary (a real load spike can't be
summoned deterministically). The lock's mtime is aged 120 s past the 30 s grace.

Fixed tree (this PR):

```
=== single-blip — openclaw doctor --fix (real noteSessionLockHealth) ===
◇  Session locks
│  - Found 1 session lock file.
│  - .../agents/proof-agent/sessions/sess-proof.jsonl.lock  pid=1479913 (alive) age=0s stale=no
transient EAGAIN reads injected : 1
lock still present after --fix  : true
RESULT: PASS — live lock preserved

=== sustained-burst (all 3 read attempts fail) ===
transient EAGAIN reads injected : 3
lock still present after --fix  : true
RESULT: PASS — live lock preserved
```

Negative control — upstream `main` (no fix), same real harness — `openclaw doctor
--fix` deletes the live lock:

```
│    [removed]
│  - Removed 1 stale session lock file.
lock still present after --fix  : false
RESULT: FAIL — live lock removed   (both single-blip and sustained-burst)
```

### Focused regression tests

Two deterministic tests run `cleanStaleLockFiles` against a valid, live
OpenClaw-owned lock aged past the grace, injecting transient `EAGAIN`:

```
 ✓ retries a transient read during cleanup so a live lock is not wrongly removed
     // single blip → retry recovers the payload → lock preserved
 ✓ does not remove a live lock when transient reads exhaust retries during cleanup
     // sustained burst → all retries fail → fail closed → lock preserved

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  56 passed (56)
```

Reverting the fix fails exactly these two tests (the null payload otherwise falls
into the mtime grace and is removed).

Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts`; full
changed-lane checks are delegated to CI.

### Follow-up

In the sustained-burst case the preserved lock is skipped from `result.locks`, so
`openclaw doctor` does not currently list it. Surfacing unreadable locks in
doctor/startup diagnostics is a small additive follow-up (touches
`doctor-session-locks.ts` rendering); proposed separately to keep this PR to the
correctness fix.

target.title: feat(workboard): refresh Control UI from live changes
target.body:
Closes #98805

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the Control UI Workboard could remain stale after cards changed through Gateway methods, tools, commands, separate CLI processes, or background dispatch. Freshness previously depended on manual refresh or optional timer polling, which is disabled by default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workboard now owns one canonical mutation-notification path and reconciles commits from separate processes through its existing SQLite store. A lifecycle-owned `plugin.workboard.changed` Gateway event carries only epoch/revision invalidation facts under `operator.read`; the Control UI coalesces those facts and refetches canonical Workboard data, including reconnect, plugin reload, visibility, protected-edit, transient-failure, and stale-write recovery. Manual refresh remains; routine timer polling and its controls are removed.

The event is an invalidation hint, not a second event log or state store. Existing Workboard reads and SQLite events remain authoritative, and no card bodies are broadcast.

## User Impact

Operators with an open Workboard see card and task-ledger changes reconcile without routine polling, including mutations initiated outside the current browser process. Inactive or hidden Workboard views defer reads until active again, and editing/mutation controls stay read-only until the canonical snapshot covers the newest accepted revision.

## Evidence

- Exact AWS proof: Crabbox run `run_d8bdc039c15d`, lease `cbx_f7d3e06a60d6`, base `5bcd25f0fb6de3cc2ba6b6a7688a9361eb355143`, candidate tree `9128d294a7273c15d1f78d5147e96bc2156720d9`; `check:changed`, canonical build, plugin SDK exports, and emitted declaration checks passed; exit 0 and automatic lease release confirmed.
- Focused tests: 13 files across tooling, Gateway, plugin services, Control UI, and Workboard; 5 Vitest shards and 695 tests passed.
- Browser proof: `ui/src/ui/e2e/workboard.e2e.test.ts`; 2/2 scenarios passed on head `945d579282f3cdbd34b396fae3b1d41a3fa1513a`. Approved screenshot/video manifest will be linked here after the draft number is assigned.
- Static proof: 30 changed files format-clean; changed TypeScript lint-clean; docs MDX clean; 5,544 internal links checked with 0 broken; `git diff --check` clean.
- Review: explicit whole-branch xhigh review reported no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings (correctness 0.93).
- iOS adjacency: the existing Workboard design/render tests passed (15 tests); this PR intentionally adds no iOS UI behavior.

### Risk and proof gaps

- Main risk is event authorization and lifecycle/revision coordination. Tests cover reserved-event guard precedence, scope revocation, plugin reload epochs, cross-process reconciliation, exact-target races, retries, visibility deferral, stale-write protection, capture races, cleanup, and no feedback loop.
- Browser proof uses the repository's mocked Gateway E2E path; Linux changed/build/export proof ran remotely on the exact candidate tree.
- Soft sequencing note: draft #98510 currently has no exact file or Gateway-event export overlap. Rebase this draft if that session-controller work lands first.

target.title: fix: avoid model-not-found fallback on OpenRouter image-input 404s
target.body:
Closes #99078

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending image input through an OpenRouter route could see missing-model fallback behavior when OpenRouter returned `HTTP 404: No endpoints found that support image input`. The model may exist; the rejected part is the image payload/capability, so treating it as `model_not_found` can produce misleading diagnostics and fallback decisions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failover classifier now recognizes image-input unsupported wording as a format/capability mismatch and preserves that classification through the HTTP 404 branch. Existing OpenRouter missing-model wording such as `No endpoints found for deepseek/deepseek-r1:free` still classifies as `model_not_found`.

## User Impact

OpenRouter image-capability rejections no longer masquerade as missing models. Users and operators get behavior aligned with the actual failure: the request included image input the selected route cannot accept, while real missing-model errors still trigger the existing model-not-found handling.

## Evidence

Before fix proof:

```text
FAIL src/agents/failover-error.test.ts > failover-error > does not classify OpenRouter image-input no-endpoints 404s as model_not_found
AssertionError: expected 'model_not_found' to be 'format'

resolveFailoverReasonFromError({
  status: 404,
  message: "No endpoints found that support image input",
})
```

After fix proof:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "import { resolveFailoverReasonFromError } from './src/agents/failover-error.js'; const cases = [['image-input unsupported 404', { status: 404, message: 'HTTP 404: No endpoints found that support image input' }], ['true missing-model no-endpoints 404', { status: 404, message: 'No endpoints found for deepseek/deepseek-r1:free.' }], ['error-object image-input unsupported 404', new Error('HTTP 404: No endpoints found that support image input')]]; for (const [label, input] of cases) { console.log(label + ': ' + resolveFailoverReasonFromError(input)); }"

image-input unsupported 404: format
true missing-model no-endpoints 404: model_not_found
error-object image-input unsupported 404: format
```

target.title: fix(find): prevent recursive re-entry in child kill via sentinel guard (#98961)
target.body:
Fixes #98961.

## What Problem This Solves

In `find.ts`, `child.on("error")` only called `cleanup()` (which closed readline), while `child.on("close")` called both `cleanup()` and `stopChild?.()`. On spawn failure or certain error paths, the child process was not killed — leaving a potential orphan.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes with a safety sentinel:

1. **`cleanup()` now calls `stopChild?.()`** — so both error and close handlers stop the child symmetrically.

2. **`stopChild` uses a `stopChildKilling` sentinel** — prevents recursive re-entry if `child.kill()` triggers Node's `error` event before `settle` clears the hook.

This avoids the risk ClawSweeper identified in PR #98854: a direct `stopChild?.()` in the error handler can recursively re-enter the kill path.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Asymmetric child cleanup in fd find tool's error handler.

**Real environment tested**: Node 22.19+, local OpenClaw checkout.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx -e "..."
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
=== PROOF: fd find-tool sentinel error/stop ===

  [error event] spawn __nonexistent_fd_binary__ ENOENT
  [error handler] calling cleanup()...
  cleanup: rl.close() + stopChild?.()
  stopChild: → kill() child
  [close event] code=-2
  [close handler] calling cleanup()...
  cleanup: rl.close() + stopChild?.()
  stopChild: SKIPPED (sentinel/killed)
  ✅ sentinel prevented recursive kill

error event: true
close event: true
stopChild called: true
child killed: false

✅ PROOF PASSED
```

The sentinel blocks the redundant second kill when `close` re-enters after `error`. No loop, no crash.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts
 (passed, exit 0)
```

**Observed result after fix**: A non-existent tool spawn triggers `error` → `cleanup()` → `stopChild?.()` → kill safely. Sentinel guards against recursive re-entry.

**What was not tested**: E2E with a real `fd` binary across all edge cases. The proof covers the spawn-failure path — the primary error scenario for this helper.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.test.ts --run` — 2 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts` — exit 0

## Root Cause

`child.on("error")` at original line 297 called `cleanup()` (rl.close) but skipped `stopChild?.()`. The close handler called both. The direct 1-line fix proposed in #98854 carries a risk of recursive kill if `child.kill()` emits another `error` before `settle` clears the hook. The sentinel-guarded approach avoids this.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Model used**: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)
- **Co-Authored-By**: Already in commit message

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Calendar v3 events.list request deadline
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to the single `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (the Calendar v3 `events.list` URL) so the calendar-driven gateway flows (`findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` → `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents`) get a bounded request deadline
- plumb `timeoutMs?` through the internal `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` helper and the two exported wrappers `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` so callers can override the default
- default to `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — two `it()` cases (one per behavior), reusing the same `startHangingCalendarServer` fixture
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `timeoutMs: 50` reject case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green
- this PR complements #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export) by covering the Calendar v3 surface in the same google-meet extension

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` (extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts:158) is the single internal helper that backs both `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`, and it calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Calendar v3 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's calendar-driven flows (the CLI `codex meet ...` command and the agent's "find a Google Meet link in the user's calendar" path) hang with no rejection.

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Calendar helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

This is the same pattern Alix-007 used in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh, OPEN, 🐚 ready for maintainer look) and the broader HTTP-timeout campaign wave (Alix-007 #102026 chutes / #102027 mattermost / #102028 qqbot / #102025 nextcloud-talk / #102050 google Vertex — all 6/8 channels opened 2026-07-08). It is the Calendar-side complement to #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) in the same google-meet extension.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 2 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/` — passed; 17 files, 196 tests (no regressions; +2 from this PR)
- PR diff: 2 files, +194/-0 (calendar.ts 5+0, calendar.test.ts 189+0)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed (the test-typecheck gap that #98322 caught is not bypassed)
- mutation check: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires` test fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green. The first test (default `timeoutMs` stays pending) is a no-false-positive guard: under mutation the default 30_000 still applies, so case 1 still passes — this is the intended asymmetry.

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real `node:http` loopback server hanging the request and the `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`-attached `AbortSignal` aborting the inner `fetch` after the deadline fires.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (reached via `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`) now rejects with an error whose `name` matches `/abort|timeout/i` after the requested `timeoutMs` elapses, instead of hanging indefinitely on a half-open TCP connection to `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events`.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` stands up a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:<random>`, accepts every inbound request, drains the request body, and never sends a response. The test replaces `globalThis.fetch` with a `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` that rewrites the production `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/...` URL host to the loopback origin and forwards the production `init` (which already carries the `AbortSignal` that `fetchWithSsrFGuard` attached via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ timeoutMs, operation: "fetchWithSsrFGuard", url })`) to a captured handle of the real `fetch`. The production guarded-fetch path runs end-to-end: `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` → mocked `globalThis.fetch` → loopback `fetch` → hanging `node:http` socket.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 2/2 tests pass; the 2 verbose test names are:
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed` (~410 ms)
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint` (~60 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed 408ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint 60ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The first test (no-`timeoutMs` default-pending) asserts, in order:
1. With no `timeoutMs` passed (production default 30s) and the loopback server hanging on the first request, `settleOrPending(pendingCall, 250)` returns `{ status: "pending" }` — i.e. the helper is **not** stuck on a 50 ms-or-less deadline and is **not** rejecting early.

The second test (`timeoutMs: 50` reject) asserts, in order:
1. After installing `installHangingCalendarFetchStub` and passing `timeoutMs: 50`, the helper reaches the loopback server and `settleOrPending(timedCall, 1_000)` returns `{ status: "rejected" }` with an error whose `name + message` matches `/abort|timeout/i`.

**Observed result after fix**: the previously-unbounded Calendar v3 `events.list` fetch from this file now rejects within `timeoutMs` ms (default 30s) of starting, with an `AbortError`-shaped error that the existing `Promise` rejection contract propagates up to the caller. The existing public function signatures are preserved — `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` each grow a new optional `timeoutMs?: number` field that defaults to 30s when omitted, so existing call sites in `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:694` (findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent) and `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:1936` (listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents) compile and run unchanged.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or TCP RST against a live Calendar v3 endpoint. The regression test exercises the simpler `AbortSignal` contract directly through a real `node:http` loopback server, which is the same shape the Alix-007 #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) test uses for the canonical HTTP-timeout pattern. The `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` wrapper is exercised by the same test via the fact that `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` calls `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` (calendar.ts:245), and the inner `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` call is the only `fetchWithSsrFGuard` site in the file, so a single regression test on `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` covers the entire chain.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active HTTP request timeout campaign wave in 2026-07:

- OPEN: #102050 (google vertex ADC, Alix-007, 🐚), #102028 (qqbot speech, Alix-007, 🐚), #102027 (mattermost REST, Alix-007, 🐚), #102026 (chutes OAuth, Alix-007, 🐚), #102025 (nextcloud-talk Talk, Alix-007, 🐚), #101649 (zalouser probe, Alix-007, 🐚), #102094 (dashscope video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102072 (minimax media, Alix-007, 🐚), #102062 (openrouter video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102089 (twilio redact, Alix-007, 🦞), #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export, this author, awaiting r1)
- This PR: extends the same pattern to the Calendar v3 `events.list` site in the google-meet extension; complements #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) on the same extension.

**Collision check**: no open PR touches the Google Meet Calendar v3 surface (`extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts`) for HTTP timeouts. Verified via `gh search prs "google-meet calendar timeout" --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all` and `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet calendar" --json number,title,state,author`; the only historical closed PRs on the surface are bounded-read fixes (OOM prevention, see #97783 Alix-007 CLOSED, #97832 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #97879 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #98355 lsr911 CLOSED) — those are a different fix shape (response body cap, not request deadline) and the closed verdicts were stale-review rebase issues, not the bounded-read fix being wrong. The single OPEN PR on the surface, #98850 (Pandah97, MERGED 2026-07-02), is also a bounded-read fix (response body cap), orthogonal to this PR's request-deadline fix.

## Summary

- Hand optional channels, network access, providers, search, plugins, hooks, Control UI, and voice/TTS setup to the agent with verified channel catalog and docs instructions.
- Preserve remote profiles, Gateway RPC wizard sessions, non-interactive imports, secondary-agent selection, legacy external harnesses, shared runtime lifecycle behavior, and the baseline-only path for bare `--skip-ui`.

target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to every `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` and `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` so the four Google Meet v2 surface sites (spaces.get, spaces.create, spaces.endActiveConference, conferenceRecords.get) and the single Drive `files.export` site used by the `attachDocumentText` helper all get a bounded request deadline
- propagate `timeoutMs?` through the exported helper chain (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, `fetchLatestGoogleMeetConferenceRecord`, `fetchGoogleMeetArtifacts`, `fetchGoogleMeetAttendance`) so callers can override the default, and through the internal `listGoogleMeetCollection` / `fetchGoogleMeetConferenceRecord` / `listGoogleMeetParticipants` / `listGoogleMeetRecordings` / `listGoogleMeetTranscripts` / `listGoogleMeetTranscriptEntries` / `listGoogleMeetSmartNotes` / `listGoogleMeetParticipantSessions` helpers
- default to `GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Meet v2) and `GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Drive files.export) — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — implemented as a single `it.each()` table-driven test with 3 cases (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) that share the hanging-server fixture, so the test file is 222 LoC instead of 281
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from any of the three exported wrappers (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) makes the corresponding `it.each` case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 3/3 cases to green

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` each invoke `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Meet v2 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's Meet-driven flows (room lookup, recording fetch, transcript/smartNotes pull) hang with no rejection. The same applies to the `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` that backs `attachDocumentText` (a slow Drive export for a Meet transcript or smartNote can hang the artifacts path).

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Meet helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

target.title: fix: deliver background task completions through owning sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Background task completion events can be queued on the real requester session, such as a Telegram topic session, while heartbeat isolation runs the wake in a separate `:heartbeat` session. That can leave the requester without a visible final or blocked completion message even though the background task finished.

Required subagent completions also had a second failure mode: progress-only child output could be presented as a successful handoff instead of being treated as blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made
The fix keeps the behaviour narrow and native:
- Background-task completion wake sources now inspect the owning session queue and bypass heartbeat isolation only for `background-task` and `background-task-blocked` delivery wakes.
- Ordinary heartbeat isolation remains enabled for non-background-task wakes.
- Required subagent completion formatting now reuses the existing required-completion terminal classifier so progress-only output becomes a blocked handoff.
- The required-completion terminal result type now encodes the invariant that blocked completions always carry a status summary.

## User Impact
Users waiting in the original requester session, including Telegram topic sessions, should receive the terminal completion/blocker path instead of losing it to an isolated heartbeat session. Parent agents should no longer treat a progress-only required subagent completion as a successful final deliverable.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
